candidates.title: Old Drugs, New Targets: Molecular Docking Insights into Repurposing Proton Pump Inhibitors for the TLR4/MD-2, NLRP3, and C5aR1 Axes in Autoimmune Liver Diseases
candidates.authors: Yıldız M, Şeker E, Altınkaya E, Poustforoosh A, Tüzün B, Ataseven H.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Autoimmune liver diseases (AILDs), including autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis, may include treatment-resistant cases and therefore require new therapeutic strategies. This in silico study evaluated proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) across three pathophysiologically complementary inflammatory targets relevant to hepatic immune injury: TLR4/MD-2, representing upstream innate immune sensing; NLRP3, representing inflammasome-mediated inflammatory amplification; and C5aR1, representing complement-dependent leukocyte recruitment. Methods: The binding profiles of four PPIs (rabeprazole, lansoprazole, omeprazole, and pantoprazole) were analyzed by molecular docking against TLR4/MD-2 (3FXI), NLRP3 (7VTP and 7PZC), and C5aR1 (6C1R and 5O9H). TAK-242, MCC950, and avacopan were included as target-associated reference ligands solely to provide structural and protocol-specific context. Their docking scores were not used as benchmarks of relative binding affinity, inhibitory potency, or pharmacological efficacy. MM-GBSA binding free energy calculations for the best score in all proteins were performed. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses indicated stable interactions for the best docking score. Results: PPIs showed variable but potentially meaningful docking affinities across the evaluated targets. Rabeprazole produced favorable docking scores within the investigated TLR4/MD-2 (−7.85 kcal/mol) and inactive NLRP3 (−9.10 kcal/mol) binding sites under the present docking protocol. The reference ligands TAK-242 and MCC950 were included only to provide structural and protocol-specific context, and their docking scores were not interpreted as measures of relative pharmacological potency. Among the PPIs, lansoprazole showed the most favorable docking score for the C5aR1 allosteric site (−6.93 kcal/mol). Interaction analyses suggested favorable hydrophobic contacts and substantial spatial occupancy within the investigated binding pockets; however, cross-target docking compatibility may partly reflect nonspecific hydrophobic accommodation rather than genuine polypharmacology, and whether these predicted interactions produce target-specific functional effects requires experimental validation. MM-GBSA analysis supported the predicted stability of the rabeprazole–NLRP3 (7PZC) complex (ΔGbind = −56.97 kcal/mol). Conclusions: These findings prioritize rabeprazole and lansoprazole as PPI scaffolds showing favorable predicted interactions across several inflammation-related target structures within the applied computational framework. These results are hypothesis-generating and do not establish target inhibition, target engagement, or therapeutic efficacy. The results are hypothesis-generating and warrant experimental studies to determine whether these predicted interactions translate into target engagement or modulation of inflammatory signaling in AILDs.

candidates.title: Oleuropein Modulates ESR2/ERβ-Associated microRNA Responses and Alters 5-Fluorouracil Activity in the Ehrlich Ascites Tumor Model: An In Vivo and Ensemble Docking Study
candidates.authors: Gungormez C, Gumushan Aktas H, Celik Z, Ergin B, Celik E, Smail H, Sulak H.
candidates.abstract: Oleuropein (OL) is widely recognized for its anticancer potential, yet its impact on chemotherapy response remains insufficiently defined. This study investigated whether OL modifies the efficacy of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and whether these treatment responses are accompanied by changes in ESR2/ERβ expression and associated miRNA profiles in the Ehrlich ascites tumor model. OL (150 mg/kg) was administered at different treatment schedules, alone or with 5-FU (20 mg/kg), and tumor burden, ascites formation, ESR2 mRNA, ERβ protein, miR-146a-5p and miR-155-5p expression were evaluated together with validated ERβ ensemble docking. While 5-FU markedly reduced viable tumor-cell burden, concomitant OL treatment substantially weakened this effect and restored tumor-cell numbers toward untreated levels. In contrast, OL administered at tumor initiation or prophylactically reduced ascites accumulation and produced distinct ESR2/ERβ expression profiles. OL also markedly altered chemotherapy-associated microRNA responses, suppressing the strong 5-FU-induced increase in miR-146a-5p and reducing miR-155-5p after prolonged exposure. Native-ligand redocking confirmed high reliability of the ERβ docking protocol (RMSD 0.242–0.411 Å). These findings identify a treatment-dependent interplay between OL, ERβ-associated responses, and 5-FU response, revealing that OL may exert both favorable and potentially antagonistic effects depending on therapeutic context.

candidates.title: One-Pot Synthesis and Anticancer Activity Evaluation of Indolo[1,2-a]quinoline-7-carbonitrile Derivatives
candidates.authors: Yimnoi K, Boosaman N, Chuanopparat N, Jearawuttanakul K, Seemakhan S, Khumpanied T, Wannalo W, Borwornpinyo S, Ngernmeesri P.
candidates.abstract: AbstractIndolo[1,2-a]quinoline derivatives represent an attractive heterocyclic scaffold in anticancer drug discovery. Herein, fifty-four novel indolo[1,2-a]quinoline-7-carbonitrile analogs were synthesized via a transition-metal-free cascade reaction involving nucleophilic aromatic substitution and Knoevenagel condensation, affording yields up to 87%. All compounds were evaluated for their antiproliferative activities against human colorectal (HCT-116 and HT-29) and breast (MCF-7) cancer cell lines using the MTT assay. Eleven analogs exhibited high potency with IC50 values ranging from 2.16 to 8.18 µM. Notably, 2-bromoindolo[1,2-a]quinoline-7-carbonitrile displayed broad-spectrum cytotoxicity across HCT-116, HT-29, and MCF-7 lines (IC50 = 3.64 ± 0.72, 5.29 ± 1.83, and 6.06 ± 0.16 µM, respectively). To explore potential binding modes and rationalize structural features, molecular docking simulations were conducted against CDK2, CDK6, and EGFR kinase models. The in silico results revealed strong predicted binding affinities (−7.73 to −9.49 kcal/mol), driven predominantly by C7-cyano hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, providing hypothetical insights into how these scaffolds might interact with ATP-binding pockets. These findings demonstrate that the indolo[1,2-a]quinoline-7-carbonitrile framework holds significant promise as a pharmacophore for further mechanistic and drug development studies.Keywords: indolo[1,2-a]quinoline; cascade reaction; one-pot synthesis; metal-free synthesis; small-molecule anticancer agents; colorectal cancer; breast cancer; molecular docking

candidates.title: Oxaprozin-Based Amide Derivatives as Multifunctional Agents: Synthesis, Characterization, and Comprehensive Biological Profiling
candidates.authors: Gogić A, Nikolić M, Nedeljković N, Vesović M, Živanović A, Dobričić V, Bošković J, Kostić I, Marinković J, Jurišević M, Gajović N, Simović Marković B, Zdravković N, Jovanović I.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inflammation plays a role at multiple levels, contributing to tumorigenesis, cellular proliferation, cell survival, and metastasis. The established link between chronic inflammation and tumor development has shifted the therapeutic focus toward nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which exert their effects primarily through cyclooxygenase inhibition. Methods: In the present study, the antitumor potential of novel synthesized oxaprozin derivatives was evaluated using the MTT assay. The immunomodulatory effects of the selected derivative were determined in vitro by measuring cytokine concentrations and performing flow cytometry. To investigate the inhibitory capacity of these derivatives against cyclooxygenase enzymes, an in vitro inhibition assay was conducted using fluorometric screening kits, followed by in silico validation. Results: All tested tumor cell lines exhibited sensitivity to compound 1, which demonstrated the lowest cytotoxic effect against non-cancerous mMSCs and MRC-5 cells. This compound can effectively target tumor cells, inducing potent apoptosis in 4T1 breast cancer cells through a strategic shift in the Bax/Bcl-2 balance and the downregulation of the oncogenic driver Bcl-6. Although the synthesized oxaprozin derivatives showed moderate affinity for COX-1, none of the newly synthesized compounds achieved more than 50% inhibition against COX-2 at a concentration of 100 μM. Consistently, in silico procedures validated the results of the in vitro COX inhibition assay. Conclusions: The findings of this study indicate that compound 1 has the ability to modulate immune responses under stimulated conditions, and its potent antitumor activity may not be directly related to cyclooxygenase inhibition, suggesting the involvement of COX-independent pathways.

candidates.title: Physiological and Molecular Characterization of Allyl Isothiocyanate Adaptation in the Formosan Subterranean Termite, Coptotermes formosanus
candidates.authors: Jiang W, Cai L, Zhu F, Moural T, Yang T, Zhang J, Zhao Q, Wu M.
candidates.abstract: Simple SummaryThe Formosan subterranean termite, Coptotermes formosanus, is one of the most destructive termite species worldwide, causing extensive damage to wooden structures and other cellulose-based materials. Although chemical pesticides are widely used for termite management, their environmental impacts have encouraged the search for safer alternatives. Allyl isothiocyanate (AITC), a natural compound derived from plants, has shown promise as an insect control agent. In this study, we investigated how termites respond to AITC exposure by examining changes in their antioxidant defenses, detoxification systems, and nervous system. We found that AITC exposure altered these physiological systems, providing new insights into how termites respond to this plant-derived compound. These findings support further research evaluating AITC as a potential tool for more environmentally compatible termite management.

candidates.title: Phyto-Mediated Synthesized Gold Nanoparticles (AuNPs) from Ozoroa paniculosa Leaf Extracts: Chemical Characterization and Antidiabetic Evaluation
candidates.authors: Cele N, Ramile K, Masikane S, Chukwuka M, Khoza S, Revaprasadu N, Opoku A.
candidates.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a serious health concern, as it remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Despite the available antidiabetic drugs used in the management of diabetes, the continuous increase in hyperglycemia has prompted growing interest in developing effective, green alternative therapeutic strategies for diabetes mellitus. Hence, this study aimed to synthesize O. paniculosa extract-passivated AuNPs and evaluate their antidiabetic properties. Methods: The plant material was sequentially extracted with n-hexane, dichloromethane (DCM) and 70% ethanol (70% EtOH), after which the resulting extracts were used to synthesize AuNPs that were characterized through various analytical techniques. The antioxidant activity of AuNPs was screened against DPPH, ABTS, metal iron chelating and reducing power. The enzyme inhibitory activity of AuNPs on α-amylase, as well as the ability of AuNPs to glycate protein, was investigated on a BSA-fructose model over a period of 28 days. Results: The FT-IR, pXRD, HR-TEM, STEM-EDS and UV-Vis spectroscopy analyses confirmed the synthesis of O. paniculosa extract-passivated AuNPs bearing faceted NPs and triangular 2D nanoplates morphologies. Despite the poor scavenging activity of AuNPs on DPPH and ABTS, a significant metal-ion chelating potential with IC50 values ranging from 76.7 ± 0.02 μg/mL to 83.3 ± 0.03 μg/mL and a good reduction potential was observed. Furthermore, an inhibition in concentration-dependent α-amylase activity was observed, with IC50 values ranging from 76.7 ± 0.02 μg/mL to 380 ± 0.12 μg/mL, and the formation of AGEs was suppressed, with an inhibitory effect observed over a period of 28 days. Conclusions: The results obtained suggest that O. paniculosa extract-passivated AuNPs possess some potential antioxidant and antidiabetic properties.

candidates.title: Phytochemical Constituents from Ardisia sylvestris Pitard Leaves: Enzyme Inhibition, Antioxidant, and Antimicrobial Activities with Molecular Simulation Insights
candidates.authors: Ha N, Pham-The H, Vu D, Tuyen N, Huyen P, Linh N, Ninh B, Anh L, Cham B, Tra N, Anh N, Rasulev B, Casanola-Martin G.
candidates.abstract: AbstractA phytochemical investigation of the ethanolic extract of Ardisia sylvestris Pitard leaves led to the isolation and identification of eight compounds, including 3S,5R,6R,9S-tetrahydroxymegastigman-7-ene (1), myricetin-3-O-rutinoside (2), phenyl ethyl-O-α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→2)-β-D-glucopyranoside (3), 2-O-(trans-coumaroyl)malic acid 1-methyl ester (4), adenosine (5), gallic acid (6), 5-(8Z-heptadecenyl)resorcinol (7), and mandelic acid (8). Their structures were identified by NMR analysis, supported by MS data where available and comparison with published spectroscopic data. The isolated compounds were evaluated for α-glucosidase inhibitory, acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities. Among them, compound 7 showed the most promising biological profile, showing potent α-glucosidase inhibition (IC50 = 7.56 μg/mL), markedly stronger than acarbose (IC50 = 151.09 μg/mL), together with moderate AChE inhibitory activity (IC50 = 14.75 μg/mL). Compound 7 also displayed strong DPPH radical-scavenging activity (IC50 = 10.04 μg/mL), comparable to quercetin, and moderate antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus (MIC = 64 μg/mL). Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed favorable binding modes and stable interactions of compound 7 within the active sites of α-glucosidase and AChE. For the antibacterial activity, substrate-similarity-based target prioritization followed by comparative docking highlighted FabI as the highest-priority candidate target for compound 7. These findings identify 5-(8Z-heptadecenyl)resorcinol as a multifunctional bioactive constituent of A. sylvestris and provide complementary structural insights into its interactions with α-glucosidase and acetylcholinesterase.Keywords: Ardisia sylvestris, α-glucosidase inhibition, acetylcholinesterase inhibition, antioxidant activity, antimicrobial activity, target prioritization, in vitro–in silico approaches

candidates.title: Phytosterol-Rich Delonix regia Seed Oil Exhibits Antimicrobial, Antibiofilm, Radical-Scavenging and Pancreatic Lipase-Inhibitory Activities: Integrated GC-MS Profiling and Molecular Docking of Stigmasterol
candidates.authors: Qanash H, Al-Rajhi A, Bazaid A, Almarshadi F, Alesefir W, Aldarhami A, Hakami W, Duhduh A, Ahmed A.
candidates.abstract: Natural products may address infection, oxidative stress and metabolic disorders. This study used gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), bioassays and molecular docking to characterize Delonix regia seed oil and evaluate its antimicrobial, antibiofilm, radical-scavenging and pancreatic lipase-inhibitory activities. The most abundant tentatively identified peaks in the GC-MS total ion chromatogram were β-sitosterol (26.35%), stigmasterol (14.57%), linoleic acid (10.39%), and oleic acid (5.82%). Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were 15.62 µg/mL for Listeria monocytogenes, Salmonella typhi, and Candida albicans, and 62.5 µg/mL for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. The corresponding inhibition zones were 28 ± 0.7, 21 ± 0.3, 31 ± 0.1, and 15 ± 0.5 mm, respectively. At 75% of the minimum bactericidal/fungicidal concentration, the oil inhibited biofilm formation by 94.95% for both L. monocytogenes and C. albicans. DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging IC50 values were 17.04 ± 0.25 and 13.17 ± 0.40 µg/mL, respectively, while the pancreatic lipase IC50 was 26.29 ± 0.08 µg/mL. Time-kill assays demonstrated ≥3 log10 CFU/mL reductions, with no recoverable colonies for any of the five tested pathogens within 3 h. Docking predicted stronger stigmasterol binding to L. monocytogenes Sortase A (−6.60 kcal/mol) than to C. albicans lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51; −3.41 kcal/mol), involving hydrogen bonds with Met63 and Arg381, respectively, and hydrophobic contacts. These findings identify a phytosterol-enriched GC-MS-detectable fraction of Delonix regia seed oil with in vitro activities warranting further mechanistic and in vivo investigation.

candidates.title: Plasmodium falciparum putative Hsp90 functionally complements yeast Hsp90 and is inhibited in an isoform-specific manner
candidates.authors: Khamitkar S, Bag M, Kini V, Singh M, Sethi B, Bhattacharyya S.
candidates.abstract: AbstractPlasmodium falciparum Hsp90α has been proven to be an antimalarial target. However, high sequence conservation between PfHsp90α and HsHsp90α is an obstacle to developing selective inhibitors against the parasite chaperone. The parasite harbours an uncharacterised paralogue of Hsp90α, namely putative PfHsp90 (PF14_0417), which has low sequence conservation with PfHsp90α. A piggyBac transposon insertional mutagenesis study has indicated that putative PfHsp90 is essential for parasite survival. However, its poor sequence conservation with PfHsp90α raises concerns about its functionality. Here, we show that the putative isoform can complement a temperature-sensitive Schsp82 mutant, confirming its Hsp90-like activity. To identify selective inhibitors against this isoform, we developed a yeast-based assay system using isogenic Schsp82 temperature-sensitive Δpdr5 yeast strains, each harbouring Plasmodium Hsp90 isoforms. Utilising bona fide Hsp90 inhibitors, we measured their in silico affinities towards the available structure of putative PfHsp90 and categorised them in increasing order of binding affinities towards the putative isoform. The top-scoring inhibitors were tested within surrogate yeast systems. Our study indicates that only one compound, CCT018159, manifests selective inhibition of the putative PfHsp90 but remains ineffective against PfHsp90α. When tested in the asexual growth of the drug-sensitive and drug-resistant parasites, CCT018159 showed antiparasitic activity in the micromolar range. Together, our study underlines the importance of putative PfHsp90 in parasite survival and merits additional research.Keywords: CCT018159 IC50 in Plasmodium, Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90α, Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90β, Plasmodium falciparum putative Hsp90, yeast complementation

candidates.title: Preparation of Antioxidant Peptides from Hippocampus Abdominalis via High Hydrostatic Pressure-Assisted Enzymolysis: Evaluation of Their Protective Effects Against Male Reproductive Dysfunction in Mice
candidates.authors: Zhang X, Feng T, Zhu M, Xiang J, Xia G, Jiang X, Gao X.
candidates.abstract: Hippocampus abdominalis (H. abdominalis) is an important marine teleost fish with diverse functional activities. Accordingly, the present research was designed to isolate and prepare innovative antioxidant peptides derived from H. abdominalis and to assess the protective and restorative impacts of its protein hydrolysates (HAPH) against reproductive injury caused by triptolide (TP) in male mice. Notably, pepsin was ultimately identified as the optimal protease among seven screened proteases. High hydrostatic pressure (HHP) pretreatment significantly increased peptide yield and antioxidant activity of pepsin hydrolysates. Subsequently, the optimal enzymatic hydrolysis conditions were established as E/S of 3% (w/w), hydrolysis time of 3 h, S/L of 1:25 (w/v), HHP pressure of 200 MPa, and 9 min of HHP time using single-factor experiments and response surface methodology. The peptide fraction with a molecular weight below 3 kDa (HAPH-1) exhibited stronger antioxidant activity and excellent stability against pH, temperature, and simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Furthermore, animal experiments revealed that HAPH-1 alleviated triptolide-induced impaired spermatogenesis and testicular tissue damage in mice, and the underlying mechanisms involve the regulation of the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway and the Bcl-2/Bax/caspase-3 apoptotic signaling pathway. Finally, through LC-MS/MS analysis, molecular docking, and in vitro activity validation, three novel peptides with high antioxidant activity (GPAPWGF, FPALLF, and LPLPLF) were successfully screened. Collectively, this study provides new insights into the high-value utilization of H. abdominalis and the development of novel antioxidant functional components.

candidates.title: Profiling Amino Acid Substitutions in Proteomic Datasets of Alzheimer’s Disease Reveals Biological Significance
candidates.authors: Zhao P, Lai S, Dai S, Zhou C, Li N, Yu W.
candidates.abstract: AbstractBackground: Amino acid (AA) substitutions in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) have been studied almost exclusively at the DNA and RNA levels, and the proteome-level substitution landscape remains largely uncharacterized. Methods: We applied an open-search substitutomics pipeline (PIPI-C with Comet re-scoring, 1% PSM-level FDR) to two independent AD brain proteomic datasets, the AMP-AD superior temporal gyrus cohort (244 individuals) and PXD013753, excluding substitutions whose mass shifts coincide with common post-translational modifications. Results: We quantified 789 substitution-bearing peptidoforms from 185 proteins, corresponding to 784 protein-level substitution events. N > M was the most frequent N > X substitution in both datasets. In an institution-stratified case–control meta-analysis, 138 peptidoforms were more and 142 less abundant in AD than in neuropathological controls. Of 774 genome-mappable events, 710 (91.7%) were recorded in neither UniProt nor gnomAD, and only five matched a population variant with allele frequency ≥ 0.1%. The unrestricted search recovered six literature-reported sites in GFAP, ACTG1, and HBB. Conclusions: Proteome-level profiling reveals substitution events in AD brains that catalogued germline variation does not explain; their molecular origin requires orthogonal validation.Keywords: amino acid substitution, TMT proteomics, Alzheimer’s disease, peptidoform identification, amino acid substitutomics

candidates.title: Proprietary Cationic Lipo-Oligopeptides Inhibit Herpes Simplex Virus-1 Infection
candidates.authors: Forte O, Ayariga J, Sahu R, Sipowe A, Owen D, Dennis V.
candidates.abstract: AbstractThe use of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) to combat herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) infection has surged amidst the rise of HSV-1 drug-resistant strains. AMPs offer an unconventional approach to combat HSV-1 infection by exerting their activity on multiple phases of the viral life cycle, while exhibiting low rates of resistance emergence. In this study, an integrated in silico and in vitro approach was used to evaluate six proprietary cationic lipo-oligopeptides (CLOPs) (P226, P359, P577, P581, OB1105, and OB1111) as potential anti-HSV-1 agents. Computational tools were used to predict various physiochemical and pharmacokinetic parameters of CLOPs and to assess their molecular docking and binding affinities for HSV-1 glycoproteins. Our findings showed that CLOPs conform to the Pfizer’s rule, predicting a low risk of toxicity. All CLOPs were predicted to exhibit antiviral activity against HSV-1 and interact with major HSV-1 glycoproteins, with energies ranging from −7.5 to −3.2 Kcal/mol. Next, in vitro cytotoxicity along with viral plaque reduction and attachment assays were performed in eukaryotic cells. Our results confirmed that CLOPs were non-cytotoxic and inhibited HSV-1 plaque formation and viral titers in eukaryotic cells. Notably, the plaques were visually smaller in treated cells than those in the HSV-1 control, suggesting a treatment effect on plaque morphology. Among the tested CLOPs, OB1111 emerged as the best anti-HSV-1 candidate, consistently demonstrating strong antiviral activity across both computational and experimental platforms. OB1111 also exerted a significant antiviral effect at the earliest stage of infection in cells. Collectively, these findings identify OB1111 as a strong candidate for further evaluations of its antiviral effects and mechanisms against HSV-1.Keywords: antimicrobial peptides, herpes simplex virus type 1, glycoproteins, ADMET, molecular docking, ligand, viral plaque assay, cytotoxicity

candidates.title: Protein–Protein Interaction-Guided Peptides Interfere with Early Zika Virus Entry-Associated Events
candidates.authors: Rodríguez-Salazar C, Recalde-Reyes D, Linares-Jiménez S, López-Cardoso C, Giraldo M.
candidates.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) remains a public health concern because of its association with neurological complications and congenital disease, yet no specific antiviral therapy has been approved. Since the envelope (E) protein mediates viral attachment and early entry-associated membrane events, it represents an attractive antiviral target. Here, we used a protein–protein interaction-guided strategy to design peptides to interfere with predicted interfaces between the ZIKV E protein and cellular receptors involved in attachment. After in silico filtering and preliminary screening, six peptides (PZ1–PZ6) were selected. These peptides showed heterogeneous physicochemical profiles, low cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity under the tested conditions, and docking-predicted interactions with functional E protein regions. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, antiviral activity depended on the timing of exposure, with greater reductions in infectious titers during co-treatment and post-treatment. All peptides also reduced titers in anti-adsorption assays, supporting interference with viral attachment or early entry-associated events. Consistently, DiOC18 fluorescence signals were reduced in a peptide-specific manner, particularly for PZ3 and PZ6. Nuclease protection assays showed no extensive exposure of the viral genome, whereas transmission electron microscopy revealed ultrastructural alterations without generalized particle disruption. Overall, PZ1–PZ6 are promising protein–protein interaction-guided anti-ZIKV peptide candidates with activity against early viral entry-associated events.

candidates.title: Pseudovirus Nanoparticles Displaying the Receptor-Binding Glycoprotein of Marburg Virus as Potential Vaccine Candidates
candidates.authors: Xia M, Vago F, Tan M.
candidates.abstract: Background: The lack of a licensed vaccine against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) calls for the development of a novel and effective vaccine strategy. Methods: We report here our development of three pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs), each displaying a MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP) segment of different lengths, as MARV vaccine candidates. These PVNPs, designated S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, were generated using our proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform. The PVNPs were evaluated for their production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. Results: Our data demonstrated that the three recombinant S-GP proteins, S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, can be produced at low cost using an E. coli expression system. The purified recombinant S-GP proteins self-assembled into PVNPs with high efficacy. Structural modeling of the S-GP1 PVNPs highlighted their key architectural features, consisting of an icosahedral inner shell and multiple trimeric GP structures displayed on the surface. Immunization of mice with the S-GP PVNPs elicited high titers of GP-specific antibodies, including IgG and IgA. Conclusions: Collectively, these data support the notion that the S-GP PVNPs may serve as potential MARV vaccine candidates worthy of further development.

candidates.title: Pyrazolate-Bridged PdCo and PdCu Complexes as Dual DNA-Binding and ROS-Driven Cytotoxic Agents
candidates.authors: Uvarova M, Kulikova V, Kozmenko Y, Revtovich S, Filippova A, Shmelev M, Sokolova D, Pokrovsky V, Kaverina A, Solyev P, Eremenko I.
candidates.abstract: Heterometallic complexes offer a promising anticancer strategy owing to their simultaneous action on multiple biological targets. In this work, we report the synthesis and evaluation of the antitumor potential of two heterometallic pyrazolate-bridged complexes, [PdCo(phen)(µ-dmpz)2(OOCMe)2] (PdCo) and [PdCu(phen)(µ-dmpz)2(OOCMe)2] (PdCu) (phen = 1,10-phenanthroline, dmpz = 3,5-dimethylpyrazole). The complexes were comprehensively characterized using a combined spectroscopic and analytical approach, including single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SC-XRD), PXRD, FTIR, UV-Vis, and mass spectrometry, confirming their structural integrity in both solid state and solution. Their cytotoxicity was assessed in vitro against colon, A549 lung, and breast cancer cell lines, as well as normal human dermal fibroblasts. The complexes exhibited micromolar IC50 values with selectivity indices up to 7. Using circular dichroism (CD) and fluorescence spectroscopy, it was demonstrated that PdCo binds to DNA, with minor groove binding (Kd = 7.6 μM) being the preferred mode of interaction, dominating over intercalation (Kd = 26.1 μM). Molecular docking simulations confirmed that the dissociated [Pd(phen)(µ-dmpz)2] fragment is capable of binding to DNA. Furthermore, chemiluminescence assays revealed pronounced peroxidase-like and superoxide dismutase-like activities of PdCu and PdCo, implicating ROS-mediated oxidative stress as a second, complementary cytotoxic pathway. Collectively, these findings highlight the dual-action mechanism of the synthesized complexes, combining DNA targeting with ROS-mediated oxidative damage, positioning them as highly potent candidates for further anticancer development.

candidates.title: QSAR-Guided In Silico Design of Piperazinylanthranilamide Factor Xa Inhibitors: Applicability-Domain Assessment, ADMET Profiling, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA
candidates.authors: Gordon P, Janiak M, Gackowski M, Zielińska-Pisklak M, Szeleszczuk Ł.
candidates.abstract: An integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor candidates. Twenty literature compounds were geometry-optimized and described using alvaDesc to construct a constrained additive multivariate adaptive regression splines model. Internal validation and an assessment of the applicability domain guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs. Ten selected analogs and two same-series references were docked to FXa, with apixaban as the crystallographic comparator. Thirteen initial 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were supplemented by two independent runs for each of PAX-M09, PAX-M15, and PAX-M18. Binding energetics were assessed using molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area (MM/GBSA), alongside in silico developability profiling. The model achieved R2 = 0.904 and an internal leave-one-out Q2 of 0.846. PAX-M09 was the strongest strict in-domain prediction, whereas PAX-M15 was borderline. Apixaban redocking yielded a root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 0.953 Å. Although PAX-M17 and PAX-M19 ranked highest in docking, subsequent analyses prioritized PAX-M15, PAX-M09, and PAX-M18. PAX-M15 showed the most consistent positional behavior across replicates and consistently favorable run-specific MM/GBSA estimates (−68.76, −70.11, and −69.42 kcal/mol). PAX-M09 and PAX-M18 showed greater between-run heterogeneity. Solubility, metabolic, and toxicity liabilities remained important. The results support experimental investigation of the three candidates without changing their applicability-domain classifications or establishing superior experimental potency.

candidates.title: R278H Substitution Reduces Mouse Tyrosine Hydroxylase Activity and Increases Susceptibility to Catechol Inhibition
candidates.abstract: Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) catalyzes the hydroxylation of L-tyrosine to L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA), which is the rate-limiting step in dopamine (DA) synthesis in the brain. Certain mutations in the human TH gene are associated with severe neurological and psychiatric disorders. The c.886C>T mutation in the mouse Th gene, which results in the R278H substitution, decreases TH activity in the mouse midbrain. Here, we compared the molecular characteristics of the wild-type (TH-278R) and mutant (TH-278H) recombinant forms of TH. Both recombinant proteins were expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 cells and purified by immobilized metal affinity chromatography using Ni-NTA agarose resin. TH activity was assayed by HPLC, and the thermal stability of the recombinant proteins was assessed by differential scanning fluorimetry. The R278H substitution markedly decreased Vmax and increased the KM for the cofactor 6,7-dimethyltetrahydropterin (DMPH4), but had no effect on the KM for the substrate L-tyrosine. The substitution did not affect the T50 of thermal inactivation but markedly increased the Tm of thermal unfolding of the TH-278H protein. The substitution decreased the IC50 values for dopamine and 1,2-dihydroxybenzene several-fold, both of which contain a catechol moiety that is also present in L-DOPA. These results indicate that the R278H substitution alters the sensitivity of TH to catechol-containing compounds. Although direct evidence is lacking, endogenous L-DOPA produced during the reaction may interact differently with the catalytic center of the TH-278H mutant than with that of the wild-type TH-278R.

candidates.authors: Liang Q, Kuang J, Wang L, Gou H, Tang D, Peng W, Wu C.
candidates.abstract: AbstractMRGPRX4, which is mainly expressed in human sensory neurons, is a key mediator of cholestatic pruritus, but clinically available small-molecule inhibitors targeting it remain very scarce; thus, this study aims to screen out novel active inhibitors targeting MRGPRX4. In this work, we performed high-throughput virtual screening of the small-molecule compound library with Schrodinger software targeting MRGPRX4, and selected the top five commercially available compounds with the highest scores from 13,144 candidate compounds. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation were used for virtual validation, and the results confirmed that all five compounds could bind to MRGPRX4, among which 6′-O-malonyldaidzin showed the most favorable binding free energy and a compact binding pocket with the lowest SASA value. We further verified the effect of these compounds on Ca2+ influx in 50 μM concentration in HEK293 cells overexpressing MRGPRX4, and confirmed the inhibitory activity of 6′-O-malonyldaidzin, whose binding interaction with MRGPRX4 was additionally verified by CETSA. In conclusion, this study identified 6′-O-malonyldaidzin as a promising lead compound for further pharmacological characterization and lead optimization, with potential for development as a targeted intervention for cholestatic pruritus.Keywords: MRGPRX4, virtual screening, cholestasis-induced itching, small-molecule inhibitor

candidates.title: SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibition through dimerization promotion by peptidomimetic inhibitors and disruption by ebselen
candidates.authors: Liu C, Jia Q, Zhao C, Yao ZP.
candidates.abstract: AbstractThe SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) is a key antiviral target that equilibrates between an active dimer and inactive monomer, making the dimerization interface a promising therapeutic vulnerability. This study investigates Mpro monomer-dimer equilibrium and conformational changes induced by inhibitor binding using 13C labeling with native mass spectrometry and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS). We evaluated how peptidomimetic inhibitors (PF-07321332, PF-00835231, GC376, boceprevir) and non-peptidomimetic inhibitors (carmofur, ebselen, MR6-31-2, AT7519, pelitinib) influence Mpro dimerization and subunit exchange. Key findings revealed divergent mechanisms: peptidomimetic inhibitors significantly shifted the equilibrium towards the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange dynamics and rigidifying the dimer interface; in contrast, ebselen impaired dimer formation and increased interface flexibility. Notably, tandem mass spectrometry identified a novel covalent binding site for ebselen at C300. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses demonstrated that this C300 modification allosterically alters the hydrogen bond network of the dimer interface, directly contributing to ebselen-mediated dimer disruption and enzymatic inhibition. Overall, this study clarifies distinct inhibitory modes between peptidomimetics and ebselen, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting allosteric sites at the dimer interface for designing next-generation Mpro inhibitors.Research organism: None

candidates.title: Screening of Bioactive Compounds in the Tianma–Gouteng Pair and Its Protective Effects on an L-NAME-Induced Trophoblast Organoid Injury Model
candidates.authors: Zhang A, Rao B, Lu Y, Liu Y, Zheng A, Liu R, Liu X, He T, Wang C, Li L.
candidates.abstract: Background: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive, high incidence disorder occurring only during pregnancy and has high incidence. The Tianma–Gouteng pair (TGP) is used in traditional Chinese medicine for cardiovascular indications, but its candidate bioactive constituents and relevance to PE remain unclear. Objectives: This study aimed to identify candidate TGP compounds relevant to PE and elucidate their effects in experimental trophoblast models. Methods: Placental transcriptomes and network pharmacology analysis were used as an exploratory discovery stage. Candidate compounds of TGP were then evaluated using ADRA1A-overexpression cells and trophoblast organoids, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and an L-NAME-induced trophoblast organoid injury model. Results: Placental injury and dysfunction were observed in PE mice. Integrated analyses prioritized α1A-adrenergic receptor (ADRA1A) as a candidate TGP-associated target. Five database-derived compounds of TGP were evaluated experimentally. Isorhynchophylline (SRH) showed direct binding to ADRA1A by SPR (equilibrium KD = 4.67 μM). In trophoblast organoids, 15 μM SRH did not significantly reduce viability and was associated with partial restoration of Ki67 and HLA-G expression after L-NAME injury. Conclusions: The data supported ADRA1A as a prioritized candidate target and SRH as a candidate compound with ADRA1A binding and activity in the experimental models. However, the current study did not establish that the biological effects of SRH depend on ADRA1A or demonstrate clinical efficacy of TGP or SRH in PE.

candidates.title: Scutellarin Alleviates Pulmonary Hypertension by Inhibiting the NF-κB/NLRP3 Signaling Pathway to Suppress Inflammation and Pyroptosis
candidates.authors: Zhang X, Xie J, Zhou Y, Gui W, Chen J, Liu K, Ma R.
candidates.abstract: Background: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive fatal cardiovascular disorder characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling, elevated pulmonary vascular resistance and right heart failure, mainly driven by chronic inflammation and aberrant cell death. Scutellarin (SCU), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and vasculoprotective properties, exhibits unknown therapeutic effects and mechanisms against PAH. This study aimed to explore the therapeutic potential of SCU for PAH and to clarify its underlying mechanism targeting NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling-mediated inflammation and pyroptosis. Methods: Network pharmacology and molecular docking were performed to screen the core therapeutic targets and binding activity of SCU against PAH. A Su5416/hypoxia (SuHx)-induced rat PAH model was established for in vivo verification, and hypoxia-stimulated human pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (HPASMCs) were used for in vitro functional validation. Results: A total of 100 overlapping targets of SCU and PAH were identified, with core hub targets enriched in inflammation and pyroptosis pathways, and stable binding between SCU and core targets was verified. SCU significantly improved right ventricular function and pulmonary hemodynamics, alleviating pulmonary vascular remodeling and perivascular fibrosis in PAH rats. Mechanically, SCU blocked NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling, inhibited cell pyroptosis and inflammatory cytokine release, and downregulated vascular remodeling-related protein expression. Additionally, SCU dose-dependently suppressed the hypoxia-induced proliferation and pyroptosis of HPASMCs. Conclusions: SCU ameliorates PAH-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling and right ventricular dysfunction via inhibiting the NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory and pyroptosis signaling cascade, which supports its potential as a promising natural candidate agent for PAH treatment.

candidates.authors: Marinković J, Jurišević M, Gajović N, Jovanović I, Marinković J, Grujović M, Marković K, Radojević I, Vesović M, Nikolić M, Tomović D, Radić G, Nedeljković N.
candidates.abstract: AbstractBackground/Objectives: Silver has long been used in medicine for its diverse effects. Coordination of this metal ion with bioactive ligands such as thiosalicylic acid derivatives allows the synthesis of potentially promising antimicrobial and antitumor agents. Methods: The in vitro antimicrobial activity of silver(I) complexes (C1–C5) and their corresponding ligands (L1–L5) was determined using a resazurin-based microdilution method, while the inhibition of preformed biofilms was assessed against S. aureus, P. mirabilis, and P. aeruginosa. To explore the binding modes and affinity of the investigated silver(I) complexes, a molecular docking study was performed against the LasR transcriptional regulator, while in silico ADMET screening was conducted using the pkCSM online platform. Finally, the evaluation of in vitro immunomodulatory effects of the silver(I) complexes was assessed by measuring cytokine concentrations and performing flow cytometry. Results: In vitro and in silico evaluations confirm that the C2 complex possesses an optimal structural balance of size and hydrophobicity, enabling superior antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity against P. aeruginosa. Regarding the immune response, treatment with the C3 complex decreased the concentrations of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-12, while increasing the concentration of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 after LPS stimulation. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate that C2 primarily targets bacterial pathogens, while C3 exerts potent immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects that differ between innate and acquired, naïve and primed immune system cells. Therefore, investigating the combined or sequential application of C2 and C3 may provide a promising strategy for the treatment of chronic biofilm-associated infections.Keywords: silver(I) complexes, thiosalicylic acid, antimicrobial, immunomodulatory effect

candidates.title: Solution Versus Suspension: How Does the Pharmaceutical Form of Insulin Shape the Mechanical Properties and Release Kinetics of a Carbopol® Ultrez™ 10/Sodium Alginate Hybrid Hydrogel with a Molecular-Docking Rationale for Diffusion-Controlled Delivery
candidates.authors: Ostróżka-Cieślik A, Ramachandran S, Marczak W.
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to determine how insulin’s pharmaceutical form governs release from a topical matrix and to provide a molecular-level rationale for the observed behavior. A hybrid hydrogel of Carbopol® Ultrez™ 10 and sodium alginate (1:2) was loaded with human insulin in two clinically distinct forms: a soluble solution (Actrapid®) and an isophane/NPH suspension (Insulatard®). Insulin release from the CU10:SA (1:2) hybrid hydrogel is continuous, without any sudden surge in release (the so-called *burst* effect), and follows diffusion according to Fick’s law. The soluble formulation released more insulin than the suspension, although the two profiles were similar in shape (f1 = 13.39; f2 = 97.54). The two CU10/SA insulin hydrogels were pseudoplastic fluids with pronounced shear-stress hysteresis and did not differ in hardness, cohesiveness, adhesiveness, or elasticity. Two rheological models, including the Carreau–Yasuda (CY) model and Santesarti’s shear rate-based model (SRB), described the recorded shear stress vs. shear rate curves fairly well. To explore this behavior at the molecular level, cavity-guided blind docking (CB-Dock2/AutoDock Vina) was performed on both the insulin monomer and the assembled zinc hexamer, using deprotonated oligomer models of the polymers. The alginate and Carbopol fragments converged on a single B-chain surface patch, where a carboxylate–Arg-B22 salt bridge supported by hydrogen bonding appeared to be the main anchoring motif, with weak docking scores (−4.5 to −4.9 kcal/mol on the insulin monomer) indicative of reversible physisorption rather than tight binding; the same patch was also engaged on the hexamer, which suggests that the proposed interaction motif does not depend on the insulin association state. These docking results are hypothesis-generating and complement, rather than prove, the experimental findings. The greater release of soluble insulin is attributed mainly to its pharmaceutical form, since the larger, less mobile protamine–zinc microcrystals of NPH insulin are likely to be more strongly entrapped in the matrix, rather than to differences in interaction chemistry. Together, the results link interaction chemistry, formulation state, and diffusion-controlled release.

candidates.title: Sophocarpine Inhibits Proliferation and Triggers Apoptosis in Breast Cancer Cells by Modulating the miR-21/PTEN/AKT and ERK1/2 Signaling Networks
candidates.authors: Shahin Y, Elguindy N, Ghareeb D, Elabd S, Balbaa M.
candidates.abstract: AbstractBackground: Sophocarpine (SC), a tetracyclic quinolizidine alkaloid, has shown antitumor potential, yet its activity and underlying mechanisms in breast cancer remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the anticancer effects of SC and the molecular mechanism, focusing on the involvement of microRNA-21 (miR-21) and AKT/mTOR and ERK1/2 signaling networks. Methods: In MDA-MB-231 and T-47D breast cancer cells, SC cytotoxicity and growth-inhibitory effects were evaluated using MTT viability, colony formation, migration assays, and flow cytometry for cell cycle and apoptosis analysis. RT-qPCR analysis, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining were performed to measure RNA and protein expression, respectively. Molecular docking analysis was performed to explore SC’s interaction with the miR-21 precursor. Results: SC treatment effectively inhibited the proliferation, survival, and migration of breast cancer cells. It also induced cell cycle arrest and triggered apoptosis in both cell lines. Mechanistically, SC downregulated oncogenic miR-21 transcription, thereby enhancing tumor suppressors PTEN and PDCD4 and suppressing AKT/mTOR and ERK1/2 signaling. Interestingly, restoration of miR-21 reversed SC’s effects on PTEN and PDCD4, confirming SC’s miR-21 dependency. Docking analysis suggested that SC may bind the miR-21 precursor and interfere with its maturation. SC also increased long noncoding RNA GAS5 while reducing miR-196a-5p and HIF-1α transcripts. It shifted the Bcl2/Bax/Bad/caspases balance toward apoptosis. Conclusions: These findings identify SC as a potential structural scaffold exhibiting preliminary anti-tumor activity against breast cancer cells, at least in part, through modulating miR-21 and inhibition of the AKT/mTOR/ERK1/2 survival network.Keywords: sophocarpine, alkaloid scaffold, HIF1-alpha, lncRNAGAS5, PTEN, PDCD4

candidates.title: Structural Compatibility and Dynamic Behaviour of Elsholtzia Ketones in the CCT128930-Defined TRPM7 Vanilloid-like Region
candidates.abstract: AbstractBackground/Objectives: Transient receptor potential melastatin 7 (TRPM7) is a multifunctional ion channel-kinase containing a structurally resolved vanilloid-like (VL) regulatory region. Elsholtzia ketone (EK) and dehydroelsholtzia ketone (DEK), major ketones of Elsholtzia ciliata essential oil, are associated with cardiovascular effects, but their molecular target spectrum remains incompletely defined. We investigated whether EK and DEK can access and maintain structurally plausible configurations within the CCT128930-defined TRPM7 VL region. Methods: The 2.45 Å cryo-EM structure of mouse TRPM7 bound to CCT128930 (PDB 8W2L; M05) was prepared in an explicit lipid membrane and subjected to restrained minimization. The workflow combined repeated M05 redocking, blind and focused docking, RICS-based within-ligand pose selection, pose clustering, property-matched decoy controls, and 100-ns explicit-membrane molecular dynamics (MD). Results: Minimization preserved the VL architecture and all 12 M05 reference contacts. Ten independent M05 redocking runs recovered native-like poses in every run (best direct heavy-atom RMSD, 0.567 Å), although these ranked only 8–10 by Vina energy. Blind docking independently sampled the VL region for M05, EK, and DEK. Focused docking identified recurrent EK and DEK pose families reproducing 10/12 M05 contacts (Jaccard = 0.833). Property-matched decoys reached comparable high-end contact similarity, showing that reference compatibility was not ligand-specific. During MD, M05 showed the strongest positional and contact retention, EK intermediate redistribution, and DEK greater copy-dependent heterogeneity. Conclusions: EK and DEK can adopt M05-compatible geometries within the TRPM7 VL region, providing experimentally testable structural hypotheses. However, docking similarity and RICS do not demonstrate affinity, selectivity, potency, or functional TRPM7 modulation.Keywords: TRPM7, Elsholtzia ciliata, Elsholtzia ketone, dehydroelsholtzia ketone, molecular docking, vanilloid-like region, CCT128930, molecular dynamics

candidates.abstract: AbstractTick-borne phenuiviruses include a diverse set of emerging pathogens whose nucleoproteins (NPs) package viral RNA despite extensive sequence divergence across lineages. We examined the NP of Tacheng tick virus 2 (TcTV2), a highly divergent member of the genus Uukuvirus. Phylogenetic analysis of an expanded NP dataset supported the placement of TcTV2 within the broader Uukuvirus lineage, and the AlphaFold model predicted a bilobed core with an electropositive groove resembling those of other phenuivirus NPs. Structural comparisons of the predicted model indicated the greatest variation in the peripheral regions. Recombinant TcTV2 NP co-purified with bacterial RNA and formed heterogeneous ring-like particles, with pentamer-like particles predominating in cryo-EM 2D classes. Truncation of the distal N-terminal region (NP152–440) did not abolish ring-like particle formation under the tested conditions. Suramin altered the thermal denaturation profile of TcTV2 NP and produced concentration-dependent responses on an NP-loaded BLI sensor in exploratory measurements. Molecular docking and a single 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation suggested a possible suramin-binding mode near the electropositive groove. TcTV2 NP therefore combines a predicted phenuivirus-like core with experimentally observed RNA association and heterogeneous ring-like particle formation, while the computational analyses nominate the electropositive groove as a candidate surface for further ligand interaction studies.Keywords: Phenuiviridae, nucleoprotein, RNA association, oligomerization, suramin

candidates.title: Structure–function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies
candidates.authors: Khlifi H, Hallab W, Mhadhbi N, Nasrallah H, Guesmi A, Khezami L, Ben Hamadi N, Wahbi H, Costantino F, Naïli H.
candidates.abstract: A novel organic–inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2− anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N–H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π–π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-metal and/or charge-transfer transitions. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations yielded a HOMO–LUMO energy gap of 2.78 eV, consistent with the observed electronic properties, while ADMET predictions suggested acceptable aqueous solubility, moderate membrane permeability, limited blood–brain barrier penetration, and no P-glycoprotein substrate liability. Molecular docking showed favorable binding affinities toward human α/β-tubulin (PDB ID: 5J2T; −5.12 kcal mol−1) and human peroxiredoxin 5 (PDB ID: 1HD2; −4.85 kcal mol−1), in agreement with the experimentally observed antiproliferative and antioxidant performances. Biological assays further confirmed moderate free-radical scavenging capacity in DPPH and ABTS tests, together with significant cytotoxic effects against HCT-116 and HepG-2 cancer cell lines. Overall, these results establish (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4] as a multifunctional Cu(ii)-based hybrid material with promising prospects for both optoelectronic and biomedical applications.

candidates.title: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, and Molecular Dynamics Studies of Novel 1,2,4-Triazole-Functionalized Benzene-Sulfonate Derivatives as Potential Enzyme Inhibitors and Cytotoxicity in HepG2 Cells
candidates.authors: Ünver Y, Türkan F, Güler H, Oguz E, Usta T, Çelik F.
candidates.abstract: AbstractBackground/Objectives: In this study, novel benzenesulfonate derivatives containing a 1,2,4-triazole ring were synthesized. Methods: Their molecular structures were characterized by IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR spectroscopy, together with Q-TOF LC/MS analyses. For compounds 5b and 5d, the available mass spectrometric data were not used for structural confirmation, and their structural assignments were based primarily on the spectroscopic data. The inhibitory effects of the synthesized compounds (3–5) against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and glutathione S-transferase (GST) enzymes were evaluated. Results: Comparison of the results with the reference inhibitors, donepezil and ethacrynic acid, showed that compound 3e exhibited the highest AChE inhibitory activity among the tested compounds, with an IC50 value of 1.60 ± 0.198 μM. In addition, compound 4a showed remarkable GST inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 1.95 ± 0.492 μM, demonstrating greater potency than the reference inhibitor. The cytotoxic effects of the selected compounds were further assessed against the HepG2 cell line after 24 and 48 h of treatment. Overall, the synthesized molecules exhibited potent enzyme inhibitory activities together with promising cytotoxic effects, highlighting their potential as lead candidates for further biological investigations. In silico analyses were performed to elucidate the molecular basis of the experimentally observed acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitory activity of the synthesized derivatives. Molecular docking against human AChE (PDB ID: 4EY7) identified compound 3e as the most favorable binder among the synthesized series, while 3f also exhibited a strong binding profile. Subsequent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations of the hAChE–3e, hAChE–3f, and hAChE–donepezil complexes demonstrated stable protein conformations and persistent ligand accommodation within the catalytic gorge. MM/GBSA calculations further indicated a more favorable binding-energy profile for 3e than for 3f, whereas donepezil showed the most favorable overall calculated binding energy. Per-residue decomposition highlighted key gorge residues, including Trp86, Trp286, Tyr337, Tyr341, Phe295, and Phe297, as important contributors to ligand stabilization. Conclusions: Collectively, these computational findings provide structural and energetic support for the experimentally observed AChE inhibitory activity of the lead derivatives.Keywords: cytotoxicity study, AChE, GST, enzyme inhibition, molecular docking, molecular dynamics

candidates.title: Synthesis, Characterization and Structural Elucidation of Biocompatible Hydroxychloroquine–Zinc Oxide Hybrid Nanoclusters as Synergistic Antiplasmodial Agents
candidates.authors: Rani S, Kumar B, Devi J, Manuja A.
candidates.abstract: Background: The increasing emergence of antimalarial drug resistance and safety concerns associated with conventional therapies necessitates the development of improved compounds. In this study, we report the synthesis of hydroxychloroquine–zinc oxide hybrid nanoclusters (HCQ-ZnONPs) by integrating a bioactive organic ligand (hydroxychloroquine) with a bioactive metal oxide nanocluster (ZnONPs). Methods: Structural and physicochemical characterization was performed using proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR), fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDAX), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential. Molecular docking against Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate reductase–thymidylate synthase (PfDHFR-TS) was performed to investigate potential ligand–target interactions. Drug loading and HCQ release were evaluated at pH 7.4. We also assessed in vitro cytocompatibility, nitric oxide estimation, total antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory and antimalarial activities. Results: The physicochemical characterization supported the successful formation of HCQ-ZnONPs. In the proposed model of HCQ-ZnONPs, a quinoline nitrogen of the HCQ molecule interacts with an exposed Zn2+ site on the surface of a ZnONPs cluster. The HCQ-ZnONPs exhibited a drug loading of 21.4% and showed approximately 48.4% cumulative HCQ release over 24 h at pH 7.4. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of an HCQ-ZnONPs nanocluster system. Biological evaluation demonstrated synergistic in vitro antimalarial activity, indicating enhanced efficacy compared with the parent drug, suggesting that this arises from the integration of HCQ and ZnO nanoclusters while maintaining favorable cytocompatibility in Vero cells. The oxidative stress and anti-inflammatory potential of the hybrid complex was also assessed, highlighting its multifunctional biological profile that may be advantageous for mitigating malaria-associated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses. Molecular docking against PfDHFR-TSfurther supported favorable ligand-target interactions and provided additional insight into the potential molecular basis of the observed biological activity. Conclusions: Collectively, the experimental, theoretical, and mathematical analysis suggests the successful formation of HCQ-ZnONPs with promising anti-inflammatory and antimalarial efficacy, establishing this hybrid nano system as a potential candidate for next-generation antiplasmodial therapy.

candidates.title: Targeted LC–MS/MS Phytochemical Profiling and Synergistic Anti-Urease Activity of Limoniastrum guyonianum Extracts Supported by Molecular Docking and In Silico ADME and Drug-Likeness Assessment
candidates.authors: Bouzid M, Berkani F, Aouar L, Sanah I, D’Elia M, Boubekeur R, Khammar H, Bensouici C, Yilmaz M, Cakir O, Tarhan A, Benbott A, Rastrelli L.
candidates.abstract: AbstractLimoniastrum guyonianum Durieu ex Boiss. is an endemic halophyte native to the semi-arid regions of North Africa and represents an under-explored source of bioactive phytochemicals. This study investigated the phytochemical composition and anti-urease potential of L. guyonianum aerial parts through an integrated experimental and computational approach. Plant material was subjected to sequential organic extraction and an additional independent aqueous extract was prepared from the raw plant; the resulting organic fractions were characterized using a targeted LC–MS/MS method validated for 53 phytochemicals. Overall, 21 compounds, mainly flavonoids and phenolic acids, were quantified, 11 of which are quantitatively reported in this species for the first time. The hydromethanolic and methanolic extracts showed the greatest phytochemical diversity, containing 17 and 16 compounds, respectively, together with high total phenolic contents (222.39 ± 0.61 and 157.65 ± 4.40 µg GAE/mg) and flavonoid contents (114.34 ± 16.82 and 223.62 ± 10.64 µg QE/mg). The anti-urease activity of L. guyonianum was evaluated for the first time; the combination of polar extracts showed substantial inhibitory activity (IC50 = 44.66 ± 1.21 µg/mL) compared with the reference inhibitor thiourea (IC50 = 19.62 ± 0.34 µg/mL). Combination analysis yielded CI point estimations below 1 across the non-extrapolated effect range (CI = 0.52–0.69 at Fa = 0.10–0.40), together with substantial dose-reduction effects (DRI ≥ 8.24 for ME and ≥1.75 for MEW). The hydromethanolic extract also exhibited preliminary antibacterial activity against Bacillus cereus and Staphylococcus aureus, with inhibition zones of 18.50 ± 0.07 and 19.50 ± 0.07 mm, respectively. Molecular docking against three urease structures (PDB IDs: 1E9Y, 4H9M, and 4UBP) identified epigallocatechin as the highest-ranked phytochemical according to the composite CNN_VS metric (3.80 ± 0.31), with an average predicted binding energy of −7.55 kcal·mol−1. In silico ADME and drug-likeness assessment further revealed marked differences in predicted oral pharmacokinetic properties among the quantified phytochemicals, with lower-molecular-weight aglycones generally showing more favorable profiles than glycosylated and highly hydroxylated compounds. These findings provide the first evidence of the anti-urease potential of L. guyonianum and highlight the synergistic activity of its polar extracts, supporting further investigation of this North African halophyte as a source of bioactive phytochemicals.Keywords: Limoniastrum guyonianum, urease inhibition, synergistic activity, LC–MS/MS, phenolic compounds, antibacterial activity, molecular docking, ADME, drug likeness

candidates.title: Targeting Cholinergic Dysfunction and Gingipain Activity in Alzheimer’s Disease: A Dual AChE–Kgp Computational Study
candidates.authors: Sait A, Day P.
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder for which single-target strategies may be insufficient. This study explored a host–microbial multitarget strategy using a CNS-oriented small molecule predicted to engage both human acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and Porphyromonas gingivalis lysine-specific gingipain K (Kgp). Methods: A CNS-focused library of 116,226 compounds was standardized and filtered to 1000 candidates for sequential AChE/Kgp docking. Refined docking, interaction-guided pose analysis, dual-target ranking, and SwissADME predictions were used for prioritization. ADKGP_0026671 was subsequently evaluated in single 100 ns molecular dynamics trajectories for AChE and Kgp, alongside donepezil and KYT-36 reference complexes, followed by MM/PBSA endpoint energy analysis. Results: ADKGP_0026671 showed docking scores of −11.804 kcal/mol for AChE and −7.345 kcal/mol for Kgp, was predicted to be BBB-permeant and not a P-glycoprotein substrate, and contained no PAINS or Brenk alerts. The single MD trajectories showed continued binding-site association and limited protein backbone deviation over the simulated period, although reproducibility cannot be established without independent replicas. MM/PBSA endpoint estimates were negative for AChE (−18.86 kcal/mol) and Kgp (−15.67 kcal/mol), but less favorable than donepezil and KYT-36, respectively. Conclusions: ADKGP_0026671 showed a balanced computational profile across two mechanistically distinct targets, supporting experimental evaluation of a host–microbial dual-target strategy in AD. These findings remain hypothesis-generating and require biochemical validation and replicated simulations.

candidates.title: Targeting FTSJ1 to Restore TP53 Function in Nonsense Mutation-Driven Cancer: Computational and Experimental Evaluation of 1,2,4-Triazole Derivatives
candidates.abstract: Nonsense mutations introduce premature termination codons (PTCs) into mRNA transcripts, leading to truncated and non-functional proteins, and accounting for approximately 10–15% of genetic disorders. In this context, the induction of translational readthrough by small molecules, known as translational readthrough-inducing drugs (TRIDs), has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy to restore full-length protein expression. However, the mechanism of action of TRIDs is still under debate, and one emerging target is FTSJ1, a methyltransferase involved in tRNA modification. FTSJ1 regulates translational fidelity and nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, and its inhibition has been proposed to facilitate the restoration of full-length proteins from nonsense-mutated genes. In this study, we investigated the inhibition of FTSJ1 methyltransferase by a novel series of TRIDs, the 1,2,4-triazole derivatives IP14, IP15, IP17, and IP18, using a luciferase assay in HeLa cells transfected with the pFLuc190UGA plasmid, which in our previous studies showed the rescue of p53 expression in H1299 R213X cells with TP53 gene harboring the R213X nonsense mutation. An integrated computational workflow, including induced fit docking, binding pose metadynamics, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA analysis, was employed to characterize their interaction within the FTSJ1 catalytic pocket. The computational results revealed stable binding modes and favorable energetic profiles, supporting the hypothesis that inhibition of FTSJ1 may contribute to their biological activity. Consistent with these findings, in vitro assays supported their translational readthrough activity, suggesting a possible mechanism of action.

candidates.title: The 3′ UTR Pseudoknot-Containing Region of Arteriviruses Acts as a PAMP to Activate RIG-I- and TLR8-Dependent Type I Interferon Responses
candidates.authors: Xie S, Zhang L, Sun Y, Shu M.
candidates.abstract: AbstractPorcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) and other members of the Arteriviridae family cause substantial economic losses in livestock. However, their pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) remain poorly characterized. Here, we investigated whether the 3′ untranslated region (UTR) pseudoknot structures of Arteriviruses act as PAMPs and explored the underlying innate immune recognition mechanisms. Bioinformatics predictions (RNAalifold, RNArtist, and RNAComposer) revealed that the 3′ UTR pseudoknot structures are conserved across all four Arteriviruses. In vitro transcribed pseudoknot RNAs significantly upregulated the mRNA expression of type I interferons (IFNα/β) and interferon-stimulated genes (protein kinase R, PKR; interferon-stimulated gene 15, ISG15; interferon-stimulated gene 56, ISG56) in Marc145 cells. Screening of RNA-sensing pattern recognition receptors (retinoic acid-inducible gene I, RIG-I; melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5, MDA5; Toll-like receptor 3/7/8/9, TLR3/7/8/9) in pseudoknot RNA-stimulated cells showed that RIG-I and TLR8 were significantly upregulated, whereas MDA5, TLR3, TLR7, and TLR9 were not. Short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated knockdown of RIG-I or TLR8 significantly reduced pseudoknot-induced expression of IFNβ, PKR, and ISG56, confirming that both receptors are functionally required for this response. Upregulation of myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88), interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7), and signal transducer and activator of transcription 2 (STAT2) suggested that IFNα/β and downstream interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) were induced via the TLR8-MyD88-IRF7 and RIG-I-IRF7 signaling pathways. Moreover, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analysis of the PRRSV pseudoknot RNA complexed with the porcine RIG-I regulatory domain was consistent with the formation of a complex between the pseudoknot RNA and RIG-I. In conclusion, this study identified the 3′ UTR pseudoknot-containing region of Arteriviruses as a conserved PAMP that activates RIG-I- and TLR8-dependent type I IFN responses, providing a mechanistic basis and potential targets for antiviral therapy and vaccine adjuvant development against Arterivirus infections.Keywords: arteriviruses, 3′ UTR pseudoknot, RIG-I, TLR8, type I interferon

candidates.title: The Architecture of Selectivity: Molecular Basis of BlTx2 Discrimination Among Kv Channels and Kv4 Isoforms
candidates.authors: Levy Y, Reis A, Blecher G, Daron O, Dadon S, Zarivach R, Zilberberg N.
candidates.abstract: AbstractKv4 channels generate transient A-type potassium currents, but the contribution of Kv4.1 remains difficult to define because few pharmacological tools discriminate among Kv4 isoforms. We investigated the molecular basis of Kv4.1-selective inhibition by BlTx2, an α-KTx15 scorpion toxin from Buthacus leptochelys. Using electrophysiology, mutagenesis, tandem-channel analysis, structural modeling, and evolutionary analysis, we mapped the determinants governing BlTx2 activity and selectivity. Substitution of conserved α-KTx residues Lys27 and Tyr36 abolished detectable inhibition, whereas N30A reduced potency, supporting a canonical pore-blocking mechanism. A Kv4.1/Kv4.3 tandem chimera reduced BlTx2 potency, consistent with a contribution of adjacent Kv4.1 subunits to the high-affinity toxin-binding surface. Channel mutagenesis identified the Kv4.2/Kv4.3 lysine corresponding to Kv4.1 Asn355 as a key barrier to BlTx2 activity, since introducing this lysine into Kv4.1 abolished detectable inhibition. Mutational mapping of BlTx2 revealed that pore-facing residues required for inhibition are separated from peripheral residues that tune potency and cross-reactivity. In particular, Q9K and I18K conferred Kv1.2 activity, partly through interaction with Kv1.2 Glu355. Evolutionary analysis linked conserved pore-facing residues to purifying selection, and peripheral determinants to diversification. These findings identify distinct conserved and peripheral determinants that together shape BlTx2 activity and selectivity, thereby establishing BlTx2 as a useful probe for Kv4.1 function.Keywords: scorpion toxin, α-KTx15, voltage-gated potassium channel, Kv4 potassium channels, toxin selectivity, A-type potassium current

candidates.title: Topical Application of Derris scandens Gel for Musculoskeletal Pain Relief and Enhanced Fitness Performance: A Randomized Trial
candidates.authors: Sungthong B, Sriphong P, Thitpraset A, Nagel A, Sripadung P, Nualkaew S, Caichompoo W, Kijjoa A, Mekjaruskul C.
candidates.abstract: AbstractBackground/Objectives: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is a common and recurrent symptom in athletes following intensive or eccentric exercise. This study evaluated the efficacy of a topical gel of Derris scandens stem extract on pain and countermovement jump (CMJ) performance in athletes with exercise-induced DOMS and assessed skin irritation in healthy volunteers. Methods: Genistein-7-O-[α-rhamnosyl-(1→6)-β-glucopyranoside] (GG), a chemical marker of D. scandens, was quantified by HPLC. In a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial, athletes applied D. scandens gel (5%) or diclofenac gel (1%) to the painful site twice daily for 7 days. Pain was recorded daily using a visual analog scale, and CMJ was evaluated on days 1, 2, 4, and 8. Changes from the pre-treatment assessment were compared between groups. Results: D. scandens gel caused no skin irritation in healthy volunteers. Twenty-five athletes completed the trial (D. scandens, n = 13; diclofenac, n = 12). Pain scores decreased and CMJ recovered over the treatment period in both groups, with a significant effect of time but no significant treatment-by-time interaction or treatment effect. Pain reduction from day 2 to day 8 did not differ between groups (MD, 1.75; 95% CI, −1.01 to 4.51; p = 0.203), nor did CMJ recovery (MD, 1.96 cm; 95% CI, −2.01 to 5.93; p = 0.315). No adverse events were reported. Conclusions: Topical D. scandens gel was well tolerated, and both treatment groups showed reductions in DOMS-related pain and recovery of CMJ performance over the treatment period. Between-group differences were not statistically significant. Trial registration: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20180608003.Keywords: delayed onset muscle soreness, Derris scandens, pain, CMJ performance, topical gel, skin tolerability, genistein-7-O-[α-rhamnosyl-(1→6)-β-glucopyranoside]

candidates.title: Unraveling Inhibition Mechanism of Structurally Distinct Flavonoids Against α-Amylase and α-Glucosidase: Insights from Multi-Spectroscopic and In Silico Analyses
candidates.authors: Li M, Mu Z, Li K, Jiang Z.
candidates.abstract: AbstractType II diabetes mellitus is a growing global health burden, and postprandial hyperglycemia is an independent risk factor for diabetic complications. α-amylase (αA) and α-glucosidase (αG) are key digestive enzymes involved in carbohydrate hydrolysis and represent important targets for investigating the regulation of postprandial carbohydrate digestion. In this study, baicalein (BA), liquiritigenin (LI), and puerarin (PU) were systematically investigated against αA and αG. Results showed that the three flavonoids inhibited αA and αG in a dose-dependent manner, with the inhibitory potency following the order of PU > BA > LI. Kinetic analyses revealed that three flavonoids exhibited mixed-type inhibition toward αA but non-competitive inhibition toward αG. Fluorescence results indicated that flavonoids quenched intrinsic fluorescence of αA and αG through a static mechanism with approximately one binding site, and the binding was spontaneous and driven predominantly by hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces. Multi-spectroscopic analyses further demonstrated that flavonoid binding induced conformational rearrangements of enzymes, manifested by the burial of aromatic residues into more hydrophobic microenvironments and the conversion of secondary structures from random coil to ordered α-helix and β-sheet. Moreover, in silico analysis revealed that hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces were the key driving forces between αA/αG and BA/LI/PU. Furthermore, abundant hydroxyl groups of PU provided additional interaction sites for hydrogen-bond formation, contributing to its superior inhibitory efficiency. These findings provide molecular-level evidence for the structure-dependent inhibition of αA/αG by flavonoids under the present in vitro conditions and provide a basis for further investigation of their physiological relevance.Keywords: flavonoids, α-amylase, α-glucosidase, inhibition mechanisms

candidates.title: Unraveling Pectin–Protein Interactions in Milk-Based Cocoa Beverages: Molecular Docking and Microstructure
candidates.authors: Akyıl Öztürk S, Habibzadeh Khiabani A, Kamer D, Karaca A, Konar N, Simsek S, Toker O.
candidates.abstract: This study investigated the synergistic effects of pectin concentration (0.038–0.462%) and homogenization pressure (5.85–34.1 MPa) on the physical and microstructural stability of milk-based cocoa beverages. A Central Composite Rotatable Design (CCRD) was employed to optimize these parameters by evaluating critical quality attributes, including water-holding capacity (WHC), sedimentation, creaming index, apparent viscosity, and colloidal stability. To elucidate the underlying stabilization mechanisms, molecular docking simulations were integrated to assess the thermodynamic binding affinities between pectin (D-galacturonic acid) and major milk proteins. Numerical optimization identified 0.40% pectin and a homogenization pressure of 10 MPa as the optimal formulation and processing conditions. Under these conditions, the beverage achieved a maximum WHC of 86.04%, complete elimination of macroscopic phase separation (n.d. sedimentation and creaming), and an apparent viscosity of 67.39 mPa·s. Mechanistically, molecular docking revealed strong, multifaceted hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions between pectin and milk proteins, with β-lactoglobulin exhibiting the strongest predicted thermodynamic binding affinity (−6.3 kcal/mol). This macromolecular complexation promoted pronounced steric and electrostatic stabilization, as supported by the highly negative zeta potential (−30.8 mV) and enhanced microstructural uniformity observed through scanning electron microscopy–energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDS) analysis. A rigorous 9-month storage study further demonstrated prolonged kinetic stability. Structural integrity was largely maintained, and macroscopic phase separation was substantially delayed despite time-dependent rheological rearrangements during storage. Furthermore, sensory profiling demonstrated high consumer acceptability, particularly for smoothness and homogeneity, with the optimized formulation outperforming the evaluated commercial counterparts. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the effectiveness of pectin in such beverage system and provide practical formulation and processing strategies for improving the physicochemical stability and shelf life of complex dairy-based dispersions.

candidates.title: VOC·BIO Library: An Integrated Platform for Published Aphid GC-MS Evidence, Biological Contexts, Cheminformatics and Exploratory OBP Docking
candidates.authors: Alsufyani T, Hussain T, Alotaibi N.
candidates.abstract: Simple SummaryAphids damage crops and interact with their host plants through chemical signals. Published volatile profiles contain useful information, but their interpretation depends on sample context and confidence in compound identification. VOC·BIO Library brings these records into one research environment. Its 11 features support data browsing, sample-context exploration, chemical structures, descriptive statistics, evidence tracing, structural similarity, networks, source references, guided questions and exploratory protein docking. Version 1.0 preserves 81 published GC-MS features across 15 contexts. It links 70 named candidate interpretations to 55 curated molecular structures without treating tentative identifications as confirmed compounds. The platform lets researchers follow a feature from its published annotation to its context, structure and computational outputs. A separate docking study evaluates 20 candidates against two aphid odorant-binding proteins. These predictions support future molecular studies and do not establish biological activity. The library is a defined, traceable starting resource for aphid chemical ecology, with broader datasets and experimental validation left for future development.Keywords: volatile organic compounds, aphid chemical ecology, cheminformatics, GC-MS, insect–plant interactions, odorant-binding proteins, molecular docking, AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, structural similarity, semiochemicals, Saudi Arabia
