candidates.title: A Biomimetic PLK1 Nanodelivery System Promotes Migrasome‐Mediated Mitocytosis to Restore Efferocytosis and Functional Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury
candidates.authors: Hu Z, Wang H, Huang J, Zhou J, Hou J, Miao H, Tan H, Wang Y, Hu H, Li N, Qiu P, Zhang H, He D, Wang Q.
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACTExcessive accumulation and insufficient clearance of apoptotic cells following spinal cord injury (SCI) are key factors contributing to persistent injury. Macrophage efferocytosis is essential for resolving injury but is compromised by mitochondrial dysfunction and lysosomal overload. Maintaining mitochondrial functional homeostasis is therefore crucial for preserving the acidic lysosomal environment, alleviating the cellular lysosomal burden, and sustaining efferocytosis. Common mitochondrial quality control (MQC) pathways such as mitophagy increase the lysosomal burden. Here, we investigated how polo‐like kinase 1 (PLK1) regulates macrophage efferocytosis and elucidated the underlying mechanism of migrasome‐mediated mitocytosis. We demonstrate that PLK1 regulates TSPAN4‐dependent migrasome formation, which drives the selective extrusion of damaged mitochondria, alleviates the lysosomal burden, and increases efferocytic capacity. To enable targeted PLK1 delivery, we engineered macrophage membrane‐coated, reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive nanocomplexes encapsulating PLK1 plasmids (MM‐NPs@PLK1). This biomimetic nanoplatform preferentially accumulates in the injured spinal cord, promotes macrophage‐associated PLK1 delivery, enhances mitocytosis and efferocytosis, supports neural tissue repair, and significantly improves locomotor recovery in SCI mice. In summary, our study reveals a PLK1‐regulated MQC mechanism that sustains macrophage efferocytosis through migrasome‐mediated mitocytosis, providing a promising therapeutic strategy for SCI.Keywords: functional recovery, macrophage efferocytosis, mitocytosis, PLK1, spinal cord injury

candidates.title: A Monoclonal Antibody Targeting mGluR2 Inhibits H9 Subtype Influenza A Virus Infection In Vitro
candidates.authors: Wang P, Xing C, Jiao S, Zhang J, Wang J.
candidates.abstract: Simple SummaryInfluenza A virus (IAV) exploits host cell receptors including metabotropic glutamate receptor 2 (mGluR2) for cellular entry and subsequent infection, rendering mGluR2 a promising target for host-directed antiviral intervention. In this study, we generated three novel monoclonal antibodies against mGluR2. Among these clones, 1G3B2, which harbours an extended heavy-chain CDR3 loop, exhibited in vitro inhibitory activity against H9-subtype IAV, markedly lowering viral titers and intracellular viral protein levels. This work describes three mAbs against mGluR2; of these, 1G3B2 serves both as a valuable detection reagent and a candidate antiviral agent.Keywords: mGluR2, influenza A virus, monoclonal antibodies, neutralization, host-directed therapy

candidates.title: A Novel Feruloyl Esterase-Producing Strain ZH-1 Belonging to Bacillus altitudinis from Baijiu Distiller’s Grains and Its Enzyme Cocktail with No Detectable β-Xylosidase Activity for Producing Functional Sugars from Arabinoxylan-Type Substrates
candidates.authors: Wang R, Yang Y, Huang M, Li X, Wu X, Zhu Z, Yang J, Wu K, Sang Z.
candidates.abstract: Arabinoxylan-rich agricultural residues are promising feedstocks for the production of high-value functional sugars and ferulic acid, yet their efficient enzymatic conversion is hindered by the complex crosslinked structures. This study aimed to isolate a novel feruloyl esterase-producing strain from Baijiu distiller’s grains and evaluate its enzyme cocktail for arabinoxylan degradation. A novel strain, Bacillus altitudinis ZH-1, was isolated and systematically characterized. Through one-factor-at-a-time optimization of both the medium and cultivation conditions, the feruloyl esterase activity was substantially increased (15.78-fold) compared with the activity obtained in the unoptimized Luria-Bertani (LB) medium. Genomic analysis revealed 103 unique carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme)-encoding genes, including endoxylanases, α-L-arabinofuranosidases, and three putative feruloyl esterases. Studies on enzymatic properties revealed that the extracellular enzyme cocktail exhibited a hemicellulase-dominated profile and no detectable β-xylosidase activity under the assay conditions, with the three key enzymes showing over 76% of their maximum activity at pH 6.0 and 50 °C. In the degradation of insoluble wheat arabinoxylan, the enzyme cocktail released L-arabinose (69.00 mg/g substrate) and a xylooligosaccharides-equivalent fraction (244.00 mg/g substrate), which together accounted for 99.57% of total reducing sugars, along with ferulic acid (1.23 mg/g substrate). When applied to de-starched wheat bran, the enzyme cocktail achieved reducing sugar yields comparable to the commercial enzyme CTec2, while producing significantly higher levels of L-arabinose and xylooligosaccharides. These findings highlight the ZH-1 enzyme cocktail as an arabinoxylan-targeting biocatalyst with no detectable β-xylosidase activity under the assay conditions, showing promising potential for producing high-value functional sugars and ferulic acid from agricultural residues.

candidates.title: A Nutrient-Dependent ANGPTL3–PCSK9-Containing Complex in HepG2 Cells and Human Plasma
candidates.authors: Bini S, Pecce V, Pinzon Grimaldos A, Di Costanzo A, Minicocci I, Covino S, Tramontano D, Piconese S, D’Erasmo L, Arca M.
candidates.abstract: ANGPTL3 and PCSK9 are key regulators of lipoprotein metabolism, with emerging evidence suggestive of a functional regulatory interrelationship. Indeed, patients lacking ANGPTL3 due to loss-of-function variants exhibit reduced circulating PCSK9 levels. This study aimed to determine whether ANGPTL3 and PCSK9 are part of the same complex. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) experiments in HepG2 cells and human plasma assessed whether ANGPTL3 and PCSK9 co-immunoprecipitated. A hypothetical interaction between the two proteins was also modeled in silico using two software packages: AlphaFold2 and ZDOCK. HepG2 cells overexpressing ANGPTL3, PCSK9, and ANGPTL3-PCSK9 were generated to investigate the relationship between ANGPTL3 and PCSK9 under different nutrient conditions. Reciprocal Co-IP experiments in HepG2 cells and human plasma showed that ANGPTL3 and PCSK9 could be recovered in the same co-immunoprecipitated sample, both intracellularly and in the culture medium. Structural modeling supported the experimental observations and identified a 2:1 ANGPTL3:PCSK9 arrangement as a plausible configuration. We observed higher association under fasting conditions and lower association under simulated feeding conditions. The latter was also confirmed in postprandial human plasma, where ANGPTL3 is known to bind ANGPTL8 in a 2:1 complex. Moreover, incubation of HepG2 cells with LDL appeared to reduce ANGPTL3-PCSK9 association. In summary, our study identifies a dynamic ANGPTL3–PCSK9 association that is regulated in a nutrient-dependent fashion. These findings may broaden current understanding of ANGPTL3 and PCSK9 biology and support further mechanistic studies, particularly in the context of therapeutic inhibition of these proteins.

candidates.title: AAV-CapNet: Multi-Omics Deep Learning with Fourier Enhancement and Cross-Attention for Predicting Infectivity of Known AAV Capsid Variants
candidates.abstract: This work builds AAV-CapNet, a deep learning model integrating Fourier frequency enhancement and cross-attention fusion, to predict the infectivity of 20 AAV capsid variants across 52 cancer cell lines with a self-built multi-omics dataset of 392 validated measurements. Validated via stratified splitting and repeated five-fold cross-validation, it extracts dual-domain capsid features fused with host transcriptomics for joint classification and regression. The model exhibits favourable performance under low-false-positive-rate conditions suitable for high-throughput screening. Attention mapping and ablation tests validate core modules’ necessity. Despite poor generalization to unseen serotypes, this interpretable tool facilitates intraserotype capsid screening and rational engineering.

candidates.title: Annexin A6 Interacts with Newcastle Disease Virus Matrix Protein and Is Associated with Reduced Viral Replication in DF-1 Cells
candidates.authors: Xu H, Chen Y, Hu S, Liu X.
candidates.abstract: Newcastle disease virus (NDV) incurs substantial economic losses within the global poultry industry. The matrix (M) protein of NDV is integral to viral replication. In this study, we examined the interaction between the NDV M protein and annexin A6 (AnxA6) in DF-1 cells. Our findings revealed that AnxA6 associates with the C-terminus of the NDV M protein, predominantly within the cytoplasm. Functional analyses indicated that the knockdown of AnxA6 expression significantly enhanced NDV replication, whereas the overexpression of AnxA6 inhibited viral replication. Taken together, these findings suggest that AnxA6 may function as a negative regulator of NDV replication in this cell culture model, potentially through its interaction with the M protein. This study offers new insights into the intricate relationship between viral proteins and host factors in NDV infection and suggests that AnxA6 may serve as a potential target for further investigation. Further research is necessary to elucidate the detailed mechanisms governing the AnxA6-M protein interaction.

candidates.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel artemisinin derivatives as potent P-glycoprotein modulators for overcoming multidrug resistance
candidates.authors: Laiolo J, Tsirogianni A, Barbieri C, Joray M, Graikioti D, Toumpa D, Lavallén J, Rodriguez N, Vera D, Athanassopoulos C, Carpinella M.
candidates.abstract: Multidrug resistance (MDR) mediated by P-glycoprotein (P-gp, ABCB1) remains a major obstacle to successful chemotherapy, underscoring the need for potent and safe agents capable of blocking P-gp function and restoring drug sensitivity. To address this challenge, we synthesized and systematically evaluated a library of novel artemisinin derivatives. Screening identified compounds A7, A12, A13, A14 and A15 as effective molecules, significantly reducing rhodamine 123 (Rho123) efflux at minimum effective concentrations (MECs) ranging from 0.19 to 6 µM. Notably, compounds A16 and A20 displayed the highest potency, with MECs as low as 0.049 µM. These derivatives also efficiently inhibited P-gp-mediated doxorubicin (Dox) efflux, with a MEC value of 0.19 µM for compound A16 and 0.049 µM for compound A20. Consistent with these findings, both compounds markedly enhanced Dox cytotoxicity by sensitizing K562/Dox cells at concentrations of 0.050 and 0.005 µM, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations and multiscale QM/MM calculations yielded useful clues for understanding the binding modes of the derivatives and identified key structural determinants and key amino acid residues that would be involved in P-gp modulation. The potent P-gp-modulating activity of compounds A16 and A20, together with the absence of cytotoxicity toward normal PBMCs at the nanomolar concentrations at which they modulated P-gp activity, highlights these artemisinin derivatives as promising scaffolds for the development of novel P-gp modulators. Collectively, the computational and experimental findings provide mechanistic insights into P-gp inhibition and establish a framework for the rational design of artemisinin-based P-gp modulators.

candidates.title: Determinants of the Nucleocytoplasmic Balance of the Cucumber Mosaic Virus and Peanut Stunt Virus 2b Proteins Regulate the Subcellular Localization and RNA Silencing Suppressor Activity
candidates.authors: Pinczés D, Sáray R, Fábián A, Almási A, Salánki K.
candidates.abstract: The 2b protein of cucumoviruses is an RNA silencing suppressor (RSS), and its activity is associated with its nucleocytoplasmic localization. However, the contribution of nuclear localization signals (NLSs), nuclear export signals (NESs), and their sequence context remains poorly understood. Here, we compare cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) and peanut stunt virus (PSV) 2b proteins and their NLS- and NES-containing regions using recombinant proteins. The subcellular localization of PSV 2b has not been characterized, and no protein structural model has been reported previously. CMV 2b displayed a balanced nucleocytoplasmic distribution and strong RSS activity, whereas PSV 2b showed predominantly nuclear localization and weaker RSS activity. Exchange of the N-terminal region and NLSs resulted in pronounced changes in localization and RSS activity. PPC 2b, containing the CMV C-terminal region preceded by PSV sequence, showed the highest RSS activity, while the corresponding recombinant virus caused the most severe symptoms. AlphaFold analysis demonstrated lower structural confidence and higher predicted flexibility in the NES-containing C-terminal regions of CMV 2b and PPC 2b, compared with PSV 2b and CCP 2b, containing the PSV C-terminal region preceded by CMV sequence. These differences may influence NES accessibility and nuclear export.

candidates.title: Effect of alkaline precipitation chemistry on morphology, colloidal stability, and antibacterial activity of ZnO nanoparticles synthesized using plant extracts
candidates.abstract: AbstractThe antibacterial performance of plant-mediated ZnO nanoparticles frequently varies despite their similar crystal structure, suggesting that additional synthesis parameters influence their nano–bio interactions. In particular, the influence of alkaline precipitation chemistry on colloidal organization and biological activity remains poorly resolved. In this study, ZnO nanoparticles were synthesized using aqueous leaf extracts of Piper auritum and Mimosa pudica with NaOH or NH4OH as alkaline precipitating agents to evaluate their role in controlling physicochemical and antibacterial properties. Four materials were obtained, designated ZnO-PA, ZnO-MA, ZnO-PS, and ZnO-MS. FTIR analysis confirmed Zn–O formation and the presence of residual phytochemical functional groups on the nanoparticle surface. XRD confirmed the formation of the hexagonal wurtzite phase with crystallite sizes ranging from 15.4 to 25.5 nm. The precipitating agent strongly influenced nanoparticle morphology and colloidal behavior. NH4OH produced rod-like particles, whereas NaOH generated quasi-spherical structures. Consistently, ZnO-PS and ZnO-MS exhibited markedly smaller hydrodynamic diameters (214.8–271.5 nm) than ZnO-PA and ZnO-MA (1448–1763 nm), together with more negative zeta potentials and lower polydispersity indices. Antibacterial activity, evaluated by broth microdilution against Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria innocua, Escherichia coli, and Salmonella typhimurium, showed strain-dependent activity, with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) values ranging from 156 to 5,000 µg·mL−1 and from 625 to more than 20,000 µg·mL−1, respectively. ZnO-PA exhibited bactericidal activity (MBC/MIC ≤ 4) against all tested strains. Overall, these results indicate that alkaline precipitation chemistry governs the colloidal organization and morphology of plant-mediated ZnO nanoparticles, thereby contributing substantially to the antibacterial performance of the resulting nanoparticles.Keywords: alkaline precipitating agent, antibacterial activity, physicochemical properties, plant-mediated synthesis, ZnO nanoparticles

candidates.title: Ellagic Acid Promotes Repair of Acetic Acid-Induced Oral Ulcers in Rats: Associations with Redox-Inflammatory Responses and STAT3/EGFR Signaling
candidates.authors: Wu J, Cui Y, Chen H, Shuai S, Zhou Z, Su S, Hou Y, Tang C, Zhang Y.
candidates.abstract: Oxidative stress and inflammation are central barriers to oral mucosal ulcer repair, yet redox-oriented interventions for recurrent aphthous ulcer (RAU)-relevant injury remain insufficiently defined. Ellagic acid (EA) is a naturally occurring polyphenol with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, but its role in oral mucosal repair and the associated signaling events require further characterization. Here, EA was selected from serum-exposed constituents of Yumai Kouyan Heji (YMKY) and evaluated using computational target prioritization, a rat model of acetic acid-induced oral ulcers, and H2O2-injured human oral keratinocytes. Network and molecular analyses identified STAT3 and EGFR as putative targets for further investigation. In vivo, EA accelerated ulcer closure, improved epithelial integrity and collagen organization, improved serum antioxidant indices, reduced serum MDA and inflammatory cytokine levels, and attenuated apoptosis. EA also reduced injury-associated phosphorylation of STAT3 and EGFR in ulcer tissues. In vitro, EA improved cell viability and migration-assay outcomes in H2O2-injured human oral keratinocytes, reduced DCF fluorescence and inflammatory responses, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced apoptosis, and regulated STAT3/EGFR phosphorylation together with Bax/Bcl-2 expression. These findings support the repair-promoting activity of EA in experimental oral mucosal injury, accompanied by improved redox-inflammatory indices and altered STAT3/EGFR signaling. The causal involvement of these pathways and the applicability of the findings to human RAU remain to be established.

candidates.title: Exploratory In Silico Evaluation of Microencapsulation Matrices for Indomethacin
candidates.authors: Vargas Rubio K, Delgado E, Cabrales-Arellano P, Gamboa Gómez C, Rojas-Contreras J, Guerrero Rivera R, Martínez Gómez V, Cordero Soto I, Contreras Hernández M, Reyes Jáquez D.
candidates.abstract: AbstractNonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), such as indomethacin (ID), may produce gastrointestinal adverse effects associated with cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) inhibition, motivating the investigation of microencapsulation strategies for modulating drug release. However, protein-based encapsulating materials remain comparatively underexplored using molecular simulation relative to synthetic polymers. In this study, the interaction tendencies of ID with cottonseed flour protein (CFP) and maltodextrin (MD) as potential encapsulating matrices were explored in silico using molecular dynamics simulations under NPT and NVT ensembles, cohesive energy density and Hildebrand solubility parameter (δ) calculations, the Flory–Huggins interaction parameter (χ), and mixing energy (Emix). The protein cohesive properties exhibited substantial force-field dependence, while the absolute χ values obtained for the binary systems were considerably higher than those reported for comparable drug–excipient systems, limiting their quantitative interpretation as predictors of miscibility. Nevertheless, within the same computational framework, CFP–ID exhibited lower χ and Emix values than MD–ID, indicating comparatively less unfavorable calculated interactions. As a complementary analysis independent of the formulation assessment, molecular docking of free ID against COX-1 and COX-2 showed a relative computational trend qualitatively consistent with published enzyme-inhibition data. Overall, the results support the use of the present workflow as an exploratory computational pre-screening approach and identify CFP as the candidate warranting further investigation among the two encapsulating materials evaluated, subject to experimental validation.Keywords: indomethacin, microencapsulation, molecular dynamics, thermodynamic compatibility, Hildebrand solubility parameter, molecular docking

candidates.title: Facile Assessment of Protein Binding Events Using a Colorimetric Dye
candidates.authors: Croskey A, Azaldegui C, Regan C, Mapp A, Burks R.
candidates.abstract: AbstractHighlights What are the main findings? The inexpensive colorimetric dye erythrosin B responds to dynamic protein concentration and ligand binding events.The colorimetric responses with erythrosin B are comparable to those observed in fluorescence assays such as differential scanning fluorimetry. What are the implications of the main findings? With a low price point and minimal instrumentation requirements, the erythrosin B colorimetric assay provides an accessible and sustainable entry into studies of dynamic proteins.The results with erythrosin B suggest that other colorimetric dyes could be deployed in a similar fashion.AbstractColorimetric techniques and their associated dyes can offer lower-cost and more accessible alternatives than their fluorescent and luminescent counterparts for many screening applications. Here, we sought to identify colorimetric dyes suitable for a presumptive assay probing protein–ligand binding, with a particular focus on conformationally dynamic proteins that are often recalcitrant to standard biophysical methods. From an array of 23 commercially available colorimetric dyes, we identified three candidates that exhibited concentration-dependent absorbance changes in the presence of two structurally distinct proteins of interest, Med25 AcID and CBP KIX. Follow-up studies of protein–ligand binding events narrowed the focus to erythrosin B, which was the most sensitive reporter of Med25 and CBP binding events with existing small-molecule ligands. Notably, binding data for Med25–norstictic acid and CBP–garcinolic acid complexes exhibited clustering patterns consistent with orthogonally measured thermostability data for each complex. Thus, colorimetric dyes such as erythrosin B may serve as more broadly accessible tools for presumptive screening assays of high-value protein targets, including those with a high degree of conformational malleability.Keywords: low-cost screening, dynamic proteins, colorimetric assay

candidates.title: Fenvalerate Induces Airway Epithelial Injury Through CHRM3-Associated NF-κB Activation
candidates.abstract: Fenvalerate (FEN) is a widely used pyrethroid insecticide with potential respiratory toxicity; however, its contribution to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)-related pathological processes remains unclear. We investigated molecular mechanisms linking FEN exposure to airway epithelial injury. COPD transcriptomic datasets were integrated with predicted FEN targets, and candidate genes were prioritized using machine-learning algorithms. Immune infiltration and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were used to examine immune associations and cell-type-specific expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations assessed potential FEN-target interactions, followed by validation in BEAS-2B human bronchial epithelial cells. Intersecting FEN-COPD genes were enriched in inflammatory, immune-regulatory, neuroactive ligand-receptor, and epithelial injury-related pathways. Eight candidate genes showed distinct expression patterns across airway epithelial and immune cell populations. Computational analyses supported a potentially stable FEN-CHRM3 interaction. In BEAS-2B cells, FEN reduced viability, increased IL-6 and IL-8 secretion, promoted apoptosis, upregulated CHRM3, and enhanced IκBα and p65 phosphorylation. Pharmacological inhibition of CHRM3 or NF-κB partially attenuated these responses. Thus, FEN-induced epithelial inflammation and apoptosis may involve CHRM3-associated NF-κB activation, providing mechanistic insight into pesticide-related respiratory toxicity.

candidates.title: Functional Analysis of Odorant-Degrading Enzymes Responding to the Repellent Activity of 2,3-Dimethyl-6-(1-Hydroxy)-Pyrazine Against Plutella xylostella
candidates.authors: Zhou Y, Wang X, Wang B, Wang Z, Li Q, Cao H, Gao Q.
candidates.abstract: Simple SummaryExtensive resistance due to the widespread application of chemical insecticides is detrimental to the green control of Plutella xylostella. In our previous study, we found that 2,3-dimethyl-6-(1-hydroxy)-pyrazine has significant repellent activity against P. xylostella, influencing the olfactory system. This study illustrates that PxylGSTs1 is a primary target responding to the repellent activity of 2,3-dimethyl-6-(1-hydroxy)-pyrazine, which was highly expressed in male antennae. Moreover, binding between PxylGSTS1 and pyrazine is mainly hydrophobic, and the TYR7 side chain is validated via site-directed mutation. These data provide novel insights into the green control of Lepidoptera insects, especially 2,3-dimethyl-6-(1-hydroxy)-pyrazine, which can be used as a lead compound.Keywords: Plutella xylostella; 2,3-dimethyl-6-(1-hydroxy)-pyrazine; repellent activity; odorant-degrading enzyme; glutathione S-transferases

candidates.title: Graphene Nanoplatelet-Modified Portland Cement: Surface Microhardness and In Vitro Fibroblast Metabolic Activity
candidates.authors: Islam MR, Caszo J, Al Razaiki K, Al Khaldi K, Al Wahaibi A, Qutieshat A.
candidates.abstract: Background: White Portland cement (PC) is compositionally related to mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) and provides an experimental platform for evaluating targeted modification of calcium silicate materials. This study investigated the effects of graphene nanoplatelet (GNP) incorporation on surface microhardness, cellular metabolic activity and mineral-related characteristics of PC. Methods: White PC was modified with 1%, 2% or 3 wt.% GNP. Surface microhardness was assessed on independently prepared discs, with three indentations averaged to obtain one specimen-level value. Day-14 MTT metabolic activity of WPS9 human periradicular fibroblasts was evaluated using direct-contact (n = 4 per group), filtered-eluate (n = 6 per group) and insert-based assays (n = 3 per group, except MTA, n = 2). Endpoint pH, cell morphology and association, vimentin-associated fluorescence, surface deposits and X-ray diffraction (XRD) profiles were assessed descriptively. Results: Surface microhardness differed significantly among the formulations (Welch’s F(3,14.15) = 190.36, p < 0.001), increasing from 44.9 ± 4.9 HV for PC to 142.2 ± 33.0, 177.5 ± 43.4 and 299.3 ± 33.1 HV for 1%, 2% and 3% GNP-PC, respectively. All GNP-containing formulations had significantly greater hardness than PC, while 3% GNP-PC was significantly harder than the 1% and 2% formulations. No significant group differences in day-14 MTT metabolic activity were detected in the direct-contact or insert-based assays. In the filtered-eluate assay, all GNP-containing formulations produced significantly higher metabolic activity than PC eluate (p < 0.001). Endpoint pH values were 13 for PC and 1% GNP-PC and 8 for the 2% and 3% formulations. Representative microscopy showed fibroblast-like morphology, cell association with the tested surfaces and vimentin-associated fluorescence. Descriptive XRD analysis of one specimen per formulation showed numerical differences in calcium phosphate-related signals, with 3% GNP-PC having the highest apatite-family classification. Conclusions: Under the tested conditions, GNP incorporation significantly increased PC surface microhardness, while filtered eluates from GNP-containing formulations produced higher day-14 MTT metabolic activity than PC eluate. The remaining outcomes provided descriptive formulation-related observations, and no formulation consistently outperformed the others across all measures. Further replicated mechanical, physicochemical and cellular evaluation is warranted.

candidates.title: Integrated structural, computational, and genetic analyses link KASII-AL263F to increased palmitic acid composition and highlight its potential in soybean oil breeding
candidates.authors: Park J, Kim K, Shin J, Lee D, Lee H, Jo H, Song J, Kim W, Lee J.
candidates.abstract: AbstractSoybean seed oil quality is governed by the relative proportions of five major fatty acids. Most genetic studies of soybean fatty acid mutants have evaluated allelic effects primarily on fatty acid composition, rather than quantifying their corresponding contents. Because fatty acid composition is expressed as relative percentage of total fatty acids, an increase in the proportion of one fatty acid is necessarily accompanied by a relative decrease in others, making it difficult to distinguish compositional shifts from changes in the actual amount accumulated per unit seed mass. In this study, we characterized PE1604, an EMS-induced mutant derived from the Korean soybean cultivar Pungsannamul and evaluated fatty acid phenotypes using both composition and contents. Sequence analysis identified a C to T transition in KASII-A (Glyma.17G047000) that resulted in an L263F amino acid substitution at a leucine residue conserved among KASII-A homologs from 11 species of the family Fabaceae. AlphaFold2 models superposed on the Escherichia coli (E. coli) FabF complex with crypto - 1b-AcpP (C16-AcpP) placed Leu263 within the buried hydrophobic core of KASII-A, distant from the catalytic residues Cys240, H380, and H416 in the active site. FoldX predicted a destabilizing effect of 6.83 kcal/mol for L263F, attributed to van der Waals clashes. Rosetta analysis also indicated a destabilizing energetic change of 11.57 REU. In F2 populations derived from Pungsannamul × PE1604 and Seonpung × PE1604, palmitic acid composition increased from 12.1% in KASII-A homozygotes to 18.1% in kasII-a homozygotes and 11.7% in KASII-A homozygotes to 17.4% in kasII-a homozygotes, respectively. In addition, analysis of fatty acid content showed that palmitic acid content in kasII-a homozygotes progeny paralleled the difference in palmitic acid content between the parental lines. Seonpung contained approximately 33.5 mg/g seed weight palmitic acid content, and kasII-a homozygotes progeny from the Seonpung × PE1604 cross accumulated 51.9 mg/g seed weight, wherease Pungsannamul conta0ined approximately 23.1 mg/g seed weight and the corresponding progeny from the Pungsannamul × PE1604 cross accumulated 38.2 mg/g seed weight. These results suggest that the L263F amino acid substitution may affect KASII-A through altered local packing and protein stability rather than direct perturbation of the catalytic site.Keywords: AlphaFold2, EMS-induced mutant, KASII-A, palmitic acid, Pungsannamul, Seonpung, soybean

candidates.title: Molecular Characterization of Soritesidine Reveals a Novel Marine Sponge DNase I-like Toxin
candidates.authors: Watari H, Nakano K, Kitano M, Kageyama H, Tanaka Y, Ishibashi Y, Sakai R.
candidates.abstract: Soritesidine (SOR) is a potent proteinaceous toxin from the marine sponge Spongosorites sp. that is toxic to mammalian cells, brine shrimp larvae, sea hare embryos, and mice. Although SOR exhibits divalent metal ion-dependent DNase activity, its molecular identity and mechanism of action remained unknown. We determined the amino acid sequence of SOR and investigated its cellular mode of action. Degenerate PCR, 3′-RACE, inverse PCR, and nested PCR identified an open reading frame encoding a 947-amino-acid acidic protein. The deduced sequence showed no substantial similarity to known proteins except for approximately 30% sequence identity to a hypothetical protein from the marine α-proteobacterium Euryhalocaulis caribicus. Analysis of the AlphaFold 3-predicted N-terminal domain using Foldseek and structural superposition revealed a DNase I-like fold with a catalytic architecture similar to that of vertebrate DNase I. A recombinant N-terminal fragment (residues 1–310, N-SOR) exhibited DNA cleavage activity, supporting the assignment of this region as a DNase I-like endonuclease domain. The recombinant fragment lacked detectable cytotoxicity, suggesting that regions outside the N-terminal DNase I-like domain contribute to the cytotoxicity of SOR. Fluorescence imaging showed that SOR entered cells and accumulated in the nucleus, whereas its cellular uptake was attenuated at 4 °C, suggesting the involvement of an energy-dependent internalization pathway. Immunostaining revealed increased γH2AX signals in the nuclei of SOR-treated cells, indicating activation of a DNA damage response. Together, these findings identify SOR as an unusual multidomain protein toxin containing a functional DNase I-like domain and provide a molecular basis for further investigation of its cytotoxic mechanism.

candidates.title: Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing
candidates.authors: Abdelsayed M, Boulaamane Y.
candidates.abstract: Virtual screening ranks compounds by scoring functions that correlate with molecular size, and hit lists are rarely benchmarked against compounds of established activity. We screened 2070 approved drugs against four Escherichia coli targets selected by pocket-druggability triage (FabI, LpxC, DHFR and GyrB), with each docking protocol validated by redocking its native ligand (RMSD 0.50–0.69 Å). Per target, the two top-scoring compounds and a reference inhibitor were simulated for 100 ns in triplicate (12 complexes, 3.6 μs). Docking did not recover the references: trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 and novobiocin 576/2069, while top-ranked compounds were large, promiscuous drugs recurring across unrelated targets. Pose triage failed, too: all twelve complexes retained 43–87% of initial contacts, contact-loss time separated targets, not compounds, and MM-GBSA favoured the reference at one target of four. Persistent hydrogen bonding separated the reference from the hits at three of four targets, by 2–9-fold, although the GyrB result rests largely on one replicate. Benchmarking each hit against its reference nominates three candidates for experimental testing: capmatinib at DHFR, metergoline at FabI and nilotinib at LpxC. Capmatinib ranks highest on these computational criteria, with the highest pocket retention (87%) and an MM-GBSA energy with no detectable difference from trimethoprim’s at n = 3 (absence of evidence for a difference, not evidence of equivalence). In this small panel, carrying a known active through the same pipeline was therefore more informative than docking score, pose stability or end-point rescoring. The nominations are hypotheses: no experimental validation was performed, and generality would require multiple actives and property-matched decoys per target.

candidates.title: Motor Deficits in a Mouse Model of Frontotemporal Dementia: Cortical Tau Pathology and Reduced Nigrostriatal Dopaminergic Markers
candidates.authors: Zadrożny M, Zadrożna P, Niewiadomski W, Riedel G, Harrington CR, Wischik CM, Niewiadomska G, Gasiorowska-Bien A.
candidates.abstract: Mice carrying tauopathy-associated mutations are considered good models for frontotemporal dementia because they replicate key features of the human disease. In carriers of the P301S tau mutation, these include degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc), reduced striatal dopamine levels, and motor deficits. Such parkinsonian symptoms have been reproduced in mouse models and are accompanied by weakened glutamatergic transmission from the motor and premotor cortex to the striatum. Here, we examined transgenic female homozygous (L66-Homo) and female heterozygous (L66-Het) Line 66 mice, which express the full-length human tau protein carrying the P301S and G335D mutations and NMRI mice as controls. Our focus was on the movement anomalies recorded using the RotaRod and Traction tests, together with histological markers of tauopathy, dopaminergic and glutamatergic systems and possible neurological markers in the motor cortex, striatum and SNpc. Compared to wild-type controls, 9-month-old L66-Homo mice presented with distinct motor impairments in both tests, which were not seen in aged matched L66-Het mice. Compared to L66-Het mice, L66-Homo mice exhibited: (1) more pronounced impairment of the dopaminergic phenotype in SNpc neurons; (2) exacerbated loss of tyrosine hydroxylase staining in striatum; (3) weaker vesicular monoamine transporter 2 staining in SNpc, striatum and frontal cortex; (4) stronger anti-tau staining in striatum and frontal cortex; (5) similar degree of degeneration in frontal cortex; and (6) similar decline in glutaminase staining in striatum and frontal cortex. Surprisingly, no tau-enriched labelling was present in SNpc in both L66-Homo and L66-Het. Therefore, motor impairments in female L66-Homo mice are associated with tau pathology in the striatum and motor cortex, together with a loss of the dopaminergic markers in the SNpc despite an absence of detectable tau immunoreactivity. Altered functional interactions between the striatum and SNpc may contribute to the observed dopamine loss and motor impairment in this mouse model. As only female mice were studied, the applicability of these findings to males remains to be established.

candidates.title: Multi-Target Anti-Endometriosis Mechanisms of Camellia sinensis Polyphenols: An Integrated Computational and Transcriptomic Study
candidates.authors: Hossain R, Jafrin R, Tangpong J, Rahman M, Sütyemez M.
candidates.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder linked to estrogen, affecting about 10% of women of childbearing age. Current treatments, including hormonal and surgical options, have limitations related to side effects and recurrence. Green tea (Camellia sinensis) is rich in polyphenols and has known anti-estrogenic, anti-angiogenic, and anti-inflammatory effects, but its mechanism against endometriosis is unclear. Using phytochemical profiling, network pharmacology, and molecular docking, we identified twenty significant metabolites. From 619 predicted compound targets and 3065 endometriosis-related genes, we identified 292 common targets that formed a connected PPI network (p < 1.0 × 10−16) centered on key proteins such as TP53 and ESR1, with components linked to estrogenic and inflammatory processes. Functional enrichment revealed key processes such as oxidative stress and cell proliferation. Transcriptomic analysis confirmed consistent downregulation of ESR1 in ectopic endometrial tissue. Molecular docking confirmed that ECG has a strong affinity for ESR1 (−7.84 kcal/mol), marmesin binds notably to PGR, and a unique EGCG–EP300/CREBBP epigenetic pathway exists. These findings outline a dual endocrine–inflammatory mechanism in which ESR1 emerges as the most strongly supported target—validated by network centrality, reproducible transcriptomic down-regulation, and docking—while CYP19A1 is nominated as a plausible complementary node, and suggest that C. sinensis polyphenols merit experimental evaluation as complementary anti-endometriotic agents.

candidates.title: PTM-PAL Pipeline: A Python Web Platform of Integrative Scoring System for Assessing the Functional Impact of Protein S-Palmitoylation
candidates.authors: Bi X, Chen J, Pan X, Tao L.
candidates.abstract: S-palmitoylation is a reversible lipid modification that can alter protein localization, stability, interactions and signaling, but detection of a modified cysteine does not establish its functional importance. Post-translational Modification-Palmoylation Pipeline(PTM-PAL) is a web-accessible workflow for prioritizing candidate S-palmitoylation sites and modification configurations for functional follow-up. It integrates site-specific evolutionary context and UniProt annotation, paired wild-type and palmitoylated structural models, local protein-body solvent-accessible surface-area remodeling, and membrane-embedding descriptors. The workflow takes site metadata, full-length sequences and paired WT/PAL structural models as input and returns dimension-resolved outputs together with a within-protein score on a 0–10 scale. Single-site and dual-site configurations can be examined separately, while the underlying measurements remain available for inspection. PTM-PAL is intended to organize heterogeneous biochemical, structural and membrane-related evidence into testable priorities; the score is not a calibrated probability and does not replace biochemical or functional validation.

candidates.title: Peptidomics and Computational Docking Prioritize Candidate Peptide–Protein Associations Relevant to Upper-Gastrointestinal Biology in a Fermented Soy-Derived Postbiotic
candidates.authors: Tremblay A, Harms C, Nankar A, Gupta R, Buko A, Tompkins T.
candidates.abstract: Highlights What are the main findings? GAD contains multiple families of overlapping soy-derived peptides characterized by extensive truncation ladders.A diversity-sampling peptide panel was linked computationally to candidate interactors spanning mucosal immune regulation, extracellular-matrix remodeling, epithelial turnover, and tissue restitution. What are the implications of the main findings? The findings support a multi-component model in which several peptide families may contribute to the biological properties of GAD, with mucosal integrity, injury responses, and tissue restitution emerging as priorities for future investigation.The integrated peptidomics and computational workflow provides a systems-oriented framework for investigating complex fermented peptide mixtures. AbstractBackground/Objectives: Gastro-AD® (GAD) is a fermented soy-derived postbiotic supported by clinical and preclinical evidence related to gastric comfort and mucosal injury. Although fermentation-derived metabolites have been characterized, the peptide fraction remains poorly defined. This study characterized GAD peptides and explored their potential biological contexts. Methods: Untargeted peptidomics was used to identify soy-derived peptides in GAD and map them to source proteins. A diversity-sampling panel of ten peptides was selected using sequence, physicochemical, and predicted structural features. These peptides were screened against a human protein-structure library by computational docking, followed by GO enrichment and context-based prioritization of candidate interactors. Results: A total of 219 peptides, originating predominantly from soybean storage proteins, were identified. The GAD peptide fraction contained extensive overlapping sequence families and truncation ladders, consistent with extensive proteolytic processing. Three literature-reported antioxidant peptide sequences were identified as exact contiguous regions within longer GAD peptides. Large-scale docking against the screened human protein-structure library combined with GO-enrichment recurrence analysis and an independent review of top-ranked docking-derived candidates identified 180 candidate protein targets spanning innate immune and inflammatory defense, protease activity and peptide processing, extracellular-matrix remodeling, tissue repair and wound healing, and apoptotic signaling and epithelial turnover. Repeated randomized-affinity controls yielded substantially fewer FDR-significant GO terms than the observed docking-derived rankings, supporting non-random functional structure in the docking-derived protein rankings without establishing the accuracy of individual peptide–protein interactions. Context-based prioritization identified 43 unique Tier 1 and Tier 2 candidates with direct or context-dependent extracellular accessibility. The prioritized biological contexts included mucosal immune regulation, extracellular-matrix remodeling, epithelial turnover, and tissue restitution. Conclusions: The GAD peptide fraction described herein comprises multiple overlapping peptide families whose prioritized biological contexts center on mucosal defense, remodeling, and tissue restitution. These findings support further investigation of peptides as potential contributors to the multi-component biological properties of GAD.

candidates.title: Prediction of Lindane-Induced Breast Cancer Toxicity Through Multi-Target Network Analysis and Mechanistic Investigation
candidates.authors: Lin Y, Xu J, Sheng M, Yang Z, Liu J, Fan X, Wang L, Xu W.
candidates.abstract: This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets associated with Lindane-induced molecular alterations in breast cancer and elucidate its toxicological mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. Lindane-related targets and breast cancer transcriptomic data were collected from public databases, and differentially expressed genes and WGCNA-derived hub genes were integrated to identify candidate targets. GO and KEGG analyses were performed to explore biological functions, while machine learning models and SHAP analysis were applied to screen potential biomarkers. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to evaluate the interaction between Lindane and key proteins. Twenty-eight overlapping targets were identified and mainly enriched in lipid metabolism, sphingolipid signaling, and p53-related pathways. The LASSO-plsRglm model achieved the highest average AUC (0.996) and identified five candidate genes, including NR3C2, AR, TGM2, ATAD2, and P2RY2. NR3C2 exhibited strong discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.982) and was consistently downregulated in breast cancer tissues. Molecular simulations suggested a potential interaction between Lindane and NR3C2. Cell experiments using human breast cancer MCF-7 cells demonstrated that Lindane increased intracellular ROS accumulation and promoted apoptosis, accompanied by decreased NR3C2 expression, upregulation of TGM2 and ATAD2, increased p53, Bax, and cleaved caspase-3 protein levels, and reduced Bcl-2 expression. NR3C2 may serve as a potential regulatory molecule involved in cellular responses to Lindane exposure in breast cancer, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying environmental Lindane exposure and breast cancer-related toxicity.

candidates.title: QSAR Modeling and Fragment Contribution Analysis of N-Benzyltryptamines at Human 5-HT2 Receptor Subtypes
candidates.authors: Đorđević V, Binić I, Petrović J, Stojanov J, Mitić Ž, Veselinović A.
candidates.abstract: AbstractSerotonin 5-HT2 receptor agonists are returning to psychiatric drug development, but separating the three receptor subtypes pharmacologically remains difficult, and agonism at 5-HT2B carries a risk of valvular heart disease. A recent study reported affinities of 46 N-benzyltryptamines and N-benzyl-5-methoxytryptamines at all three human subtypes and analyzed them with an additive substituent model, which gave fragment coefficients of the same sign at every subtype and suggested that selectivity within this scaffold would be hard to achieve. We revisited that conclusion with non-additive models built under a protocol designed for small datasets: fifty stratified partitions with all filtering and hyperparameter tuning inside each training set, external statistics reported as distributions, response permutation on three partitions per endpoint, and partitions that withhold an entire scaffold or an entire substitution position. We repeated the analysis with two descriptor sets that share no variables and are built on different principles. Penalized linear models were predictive and transferable, whereas gradient boosting reproduced the training set exactly, and neither tree ensemble transferred to a held-out scaffold. Fragment contributions at 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C correlated at 0.25 compared with 0.77 for whole-molecule affinities, and both descriptor sets gave the same figure within 0.01. All models failed on para-substituted analogs, which distance-based applicability-domain criteria did not flag, whereas models trained without the ortho or the meta block stayed above a mean-predictor baseline. Aggregation over the whole molecule, rather than descriptor choice, conceals subtype divergence. One group drives the divergence: the N-benzyl substituent raises the predicted 5-HT2A affinity and lowers the predicted 5-HT2C affinity; excluding it raised the correlation to 0.93.Keywords: 5-HT2 receptors, N-benzyltryptamines, quantitative structure-activity relationships, simplex descriptors, model interpretation, applicability domain, non-additivity, subtype selectivity

candidates.title: RapidMetalFF-AI: An AI-Assisted Web Server for Minute-Scale Bonded Force-Field Parameterization and Structural Validation of Metal-Containing Molecules with Validated AMBER and Converted GROMACS/CHARMM Outputs
candidates.abstract: AbstractAutomated bonded-force-field generation for metal-containing molecular systems remains a practical bottleneck because it is expertise-intensive and computationally demanding. RapidMetalFF-AI converts this fragmented process into a minute-scale automated web pipeline integrating an Advanced Numbering System (ANS), machine learning-based geometry optimization and Hessian generation, rapid charge assignment, bonded-parameter generation, minimization, and structural validation. The platform produces bonded parameters, assembled AMBER topology/coordinates, converted GROMACS/CHARMM representations, structural-retention metrics, and ANS-SMILES identifiers. In a deliberately heterogeneous stress test of 90 unedited CSD-derived MOL2 structures, 82 completed the full workflow and 72 contained recognized metal-site subsets. Median native/Hybrid optimized-reference global RMSDs were 0.430/0.415 Å, and metal-site medians were 0.079/0.107 Å. Relative to experimental CSD geometries, final native RapidMetalFF global/metal-site medians were 0.626/0.176 Å; corresponding Hybrid values were 0.623/0.166 Å. Nine representative systems with completed independent HF/SDD optimizations gave median native heavy-atom and metal-site RMSDs of 0.333 and 0.101 Å, a median metal–ligand bond-length MAE of 0.074 Å, and a median coordination-angle MAE of 2.865°. Ten explicit-water, periodic boundary MD tests (5 ns production after heating and equilibration; 50 ns total production) gave median time-averaged global and metal-site RMSDs of 0.571 and 0.112 Å relative to their production-start structures. These additional tests assess local geometry and nanosecond-timescale dynamical stability; they do not establish free-energy, spectroscopic, or general production-MD accuracy. For the 82 completed benchmark structures, the mean and median end-to-end runtimes were 65.5 and 48.9 s per molecule on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA Corporation, Santa Clara, CA, USA).Keywords: force fields, AI-assisted parameterization, machine learning hessian, seminario method, ANS-SMILES, GAFF2, AMBER, OpenMM, web server, Orbmol-v2

candidates.title: Saponin-Mediated Isolation of Megacomplexes of the Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation System
candidates.authors: Peng C, Hu P, Li G, Wang M, Duan Z.
candidates.abstract: Simple SummaryCurrent in vitro isolation methods for the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation system yield only supercomplexes and individual free complexes, leaving the native assembly of these complexes uncertain. The present study aimed to develop a novel reagent for the efficient extraction of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation megacomplexes, thereby enabling elucidation of their physiological assembly state. Using a native saponin reagent, we extracted numerous oxidative phosphorylation megacomplexes comprising respiratory complexes and ATP synthases. Subsequent analysis concluded that these megacomplexes constitute the dominant functional units of the mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation system. Furthermore, using these optimized procedures, we successfully isolated and characterized a higher-order oxidative phosphorylation megacomplex comprising all five oxidative phosphorylation complexes from rat liver mitochondria. Collectively, these findings suggest that oxidative phosphorylation megacomplexes may represent the primary architectural organization of the oxidative phosphorylation system, and they highlight the potential of Sapindus saponaria saponins (SASS) as a promising reagent for isolating and purifying large membrane protein supercomplexes in vitro.

candidates.title: Solidification of Lithium Slag via Microbial-Induced Carbonate Precipitation Mediated by Urease-Producing Bacteria
candidates.authors: Dong W, Wang L, Lei S, Song Y, Zhou Q.
candidates.abstract: AbstractThe rapid development of the new energy industry has led to a sharp increase in the demand for lithium resources, resulting in a substantial accumulation of lithium smelting residue (lithium slag). Conventional disposal methods like landfilling and open-air storage may cause potential environmental concerns, including the migration of soluble components and long-term ecological risks. Microbial-induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) presents an alternative biologically based stabilization strategy for waste stabilization by leveraging biomineralization to convert reactive components into stable precipitates. Herein, the feasibility of solidifying lithium slag (LS) via MICP was investigated using urease-producing bacteria with contrasting enzyme activities, including a laboratory-isolated strain Lysinibacillus sp. WD018 and a commercial strain Sporosarcina pasteurii (S. pasteurii). Due to its superior urease activity (45.25 vs. 2.25 mM/min/OD600), S. pasteurii induced markedly greater carbonate precipitation, resulting in higher CaCO3 production and the formation of more crystalline calcite. Among the tested conditions, a cylindrical flow-through mold, 1 M cementation solution, and seven treatment cycles were favorable for producing intact LS specimens. X-ray diffraction (XRD) indicated calcite formation after MICP treatment, and S. pasteurii yielded more crystalline calcite than WD018. The CaCO3 content was higher in the upper section (51 ± 0.91% for S. pasteurii vs. 32 ± 0.10% for WD018). Untreated LS had permeability coefficients of (1.71 × 10−6)~(1.13 × 10−5) m/s, whereas treated specimens showed no visible water seepage during a 30 min constant-head test. These findings indicated that bacterial urease activity and flow-through treatment configuration are important factors controlling carbonate precipitation and LS stabilization.Keywords: urease-producing bacteria, lithium slag, biocementation, crystalline calcite, stabilization

candidates.title: Spatial Metabolomics-Based Integrated Analysis Provides Evidence for the Mechanism of Salvianolic Acid A-Induced Mitochondrial Apoptosis in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer via the ROS-Dependent Caspase Pathway
candidates.authors: Jiang R, Xiang H, Xie L, Zhao L, Zeng D, Zhang Y, Xie J, Pan Z, Gong Y, Yang L.
candidates.abstract: AbstractSalvianolic acid A (SAA) exhibits antitumor activity against non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the metabolic regulatory mechanisms underlying its effects remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI), network pharmacology, molecular docking, and functional validation to investigate the effects of SAA on NSCLC. SAA inhibited H1299 cell viability, migration, and invasion and induced apoptosis. DESI-MSI analysis of xenograft tumor tissues revealed marked metabolic alterations after SAA treatment, including changes in ceramides, glycerophospholipids, and arachidonic acid candidates. Network pharmacology and molecular docking further suggested the involvement of oxidative stress- and apoptosis-related pathways. Functionally, SAA increased intracellular ROS levels, impaired mitochondrial function, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. Treatment with the ROS scavenger NAC partially reversed SAA-induced ROS accumulation, loss of cell viability, and increased levels of cleaved Caspase-9 and Caspase-3. Consistently, Western blotting and immunofluorescence analyses showed concentration-dependent activation of Caspase-9 and Caspase-3, whereas the pan-caspase inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK significantly attenuated SAA-induced cell death and apoptosis. Collectively, these findings provide evidence that SAA induces metabolic remodeling and promotes ROS-associated mitochondrial dysfunction and caspase-mediated apoptosis in NSCLC, thereby suggesting a potential metabolic mechanism underlying its antitumor activity.Keywords: Salvianolic acid A, spatial metabolomics, mass spectrometry imaging, network pharmacology, non-small cell lung cancer, mitochondrial apoptosis

candidates.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of a Marine Steroidal Alkaloid Analog (3S)-Peniadenisteroid A
candidates.authors: Zhang X, Wang X, Maimaitiming M, Yang J, Wang J, Gao D, Yang L, Zhang X, Liu Z, Wang P, Wang C.
candidates.abstract: Peniadenisteroid A, also known as striasteroid C, is a unique marine-derived natural steroidal alkaloid with a characteristic adenine–steroid hybrid scaffold, in which an adenine moiety is bound to the C-3 position of the steroid skeleton. This natural metabolite displays evident antiviral activity through neuraminidase inhibition, with an IC50 value of 6.15 μM. In this work, the C-3 epimer, (3S)-peniadenisteroid A, was successfully synthesized in eight steps with an overall yield of 3.9%. Biological screening results revealed that the intermediate (3S)-P6 exhibited prominent inhibitory activity against cellular nitric oxide (NO) production, while both (3S)-peniadenisteroid A and peniadenisteroid A presented weak anti-inflammatory effects. Further mechanistic studies indicated that (3S)-P6 exerts significant anti-inflammatory bioactivity by negatively regulating the STAT3/NF-κB and HIF-1α signaling pathways. Moreover, network pharmacology combined with molecular docking predicted Heat Shock Protein 90α (HSP90α) as the putative binding target of (3S)-P6. Overall, this study completes the synthesis and biological evaluation of (3S)-peniadenisteroid A, highlighting that intermediate (3S)-P6 is a valuable lead compound for further anti-inflammatory drug discovery.

candidates.title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of pyridine-based derivatives as potential inhibitors of Leishmania major propagation
candidates.authors: Sabt A, Bekhit A, Farag H, Jawad H, Amagase K, Ibrahim H, Ibrahim T, Elshamy A, Shaldam M, Eldehna W.
candidates.abstract: AbstractLeishmaniasis is a neglected tropical disease for which current treatment options remain severely limited and associated with considerable toxicity, underscoring the urgent need for novel therapeutic agents with innovative chemical structures. To address this gap, we designed, synthesized, and tested a series of fourteen hybrid molecules (3a–g and 5a–g) that combine a pyridine core with either thiosemicarbazone or thiazolidinone functionalities, and evaluated their activity against Leishmania major in vitro. Among these, the pyridine–thiazolidinone hybrids (5a–g) demonstrated numerically better efficacy compared to their pyridine–thiosemicarbazone counterparts (3a–g). Significantly, compound 5e emerged as a promising dual-stage agent, demonstrated to be effective against both promastigote forms (IC50 = 8.42 ± 0.14 µM), which is comparable to the reference drug miltefosine (IC50 = 7.83 µM), and axenic amastigotes forms (IC50 = 8.88 ± 0.16 µM), similarly aligned with the activity of miltefosine (IC50 = 8.07 µM). Mechanistic exploration via a folate-reversal assay pointed to an antifolate mode of action, proposed, modeling-supported target enzymes DHFR-TS and PTR1. Parasite viability was restored in a dose–responsive manner when co-administered with folic or folinic acid, with recovery rates reaching up to 74% at 20 µM and 83% at 100 µM folic acid, depending on the compound assessed. Additionally, 5e exhibited a favorable in vitro cytotoxicity profile in VERO cells (CC50 = 393.04 µM; selectivity index = 46.63). To gain further insight, molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were carried out to explore the possible binding interactions and dynamic stability of 5e within the PTR1 active site. These computational analyses support the compound's proposed inhibitory capacity against Lm-PTR1. Collectively, our results introduce a promising new class of antileishmanial agents that act through selective disruption of the folate biosynthesis pathway, highlighting their considerable therapeutic promise in the fight against leishmaniasis.

candidates.title: Virucidal Potential of Citric Acid, Lemon Juice and Lemon Essential Oil Against Influenza D Virus
candidates.authors: Falsini A, Fiori A, Cataldini S, Finetti F, Gentile M, Nardin R, Tamasi G, Rossi C, Lupetti P, Camero M, Montomoli E, Trombetta C.
candidates.abstract: AbstractInfluenza D virus (IDV) is an emerging pathogen with zoonotic potential. Epidemiological and serological evidence suggests that cattle serve as the natural reservoir, with periodic spillover events to other animal hosts. This study evaluates the in vitro activity of lemon juice (LJ) and lemon essential oil (LEO) against two IDV lineages (D/660 and D/OK). Compound cytotoxicity was evaluated on MDCK cells by measuring cell viability with a fluorescein diacetate assay. Viral suspensions were pre-treated with the compounds, and the viral titers were determined by TCID50. Immunofluorescence analysis was performed to evaluate viral nucleoprotein expression. Then, the potential morphological changes in treated viral particles were investigated with transmission electron microscopy. Both LJ and LEO showed significant dose- and time-dependent antiviral effects, leading to a rapid reduction in viral titers at higher concentrations and at non-cytotoxic levels. Moreover, at the highest non-cytotoxic dilutions, prolonged exposure (30–60 min) resulted in a reduction of approximately 1–1.5 log10 TCID50/mL in viral titers. Moreover, treatments reduced viral nucleoprotein expression and were associated with morphological alterations of viral particles observed by transmission electron microscopy, providing supportive evidence for a possible direct effect on virion integrity. These findings suggest that lemon-derived compounds possess promising properties against IDV and may represent potential natural agents for disinfectant or virucidal applications.Keywords: influenza D virus, lemon essential oil, lemon juice, natural antiviral
